title.zh: 卷五十二 列傳第二: 后妃下
title.raw: 卷五十二 列傳第二: 后妃下 Volume 52 Biographies 2: Empresses and Consorts 2

sentences.zh: 蕭銑蕭銑，後梁宣帝曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xiao Xian — Xiao Xian was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of Later Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xian was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of the Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 祖岩，隋開皇初叛隋降於陳，陳亡，為文帝所誅。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan, at the beginning of Kaihuang under the Sui, rebelled against Sui and surrendered to Chen; when Chen perished, he was executed by Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan had defected from Sui to Chen at the start of the Kaihuang era; after Chen's fall, Emperor Wen of Sui had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 銑少孤貧，傭書自給，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xian in his youth was orphaned and poor; he supported himself by hiring out as a copyist and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, Xian earned his living as a copyist and won renown for his devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，以外戚擢授羅川令。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yang, through his status as a maternal relative of the imperial house he was promoted and appointed magistrate of Luochuan.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Yang, he was elevated on account of his imperial connections and appointed magistrate of Luochuan.

sentences.zh: 大業十三年，岳州校尉董景珍、雷世猛，旅帥鄭文秀、許玄徹、萬瓚、徐德基、郭華，沔州人張繡等同謀叛隋。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daye, Yuezhou commandant Dong Jingzhen and Lei Shimeng, brigade leaders Zheng Wenxiu, Xu Xuanzhe, Wan Chan, Xu Diji, and Guo Hua, and Zhang Xiu of Mianzhou and others jointly plotted to rebel against Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daye, the Yuezhou commandant Dong Jingzhen and Lei Shimeng, together with the brigade leaders Zheng Wenxiu, Xu Xuanzhe, Wan Chan, Xu Diji, and Guo Hua, Zhang Xiu of Mianzhou, and others, conspired to rise against the Sui.

sentences.zh: 郡縣官屬眾欲推景珍為主，景珍曰：「吾素寒賤，雖假名號，眾必不從。

translations.literal: The officials of the commandery and counties, with the multitude, wished to make Jingzhen their leader; Jingzhen said: "I have always been poor and lowly; even if I borrow a title, the masses surely will not follow.
translations.idiomatic: The local officials and populace wanted to make Jingzhen their leader, but he said, "I have always been poor and obscure; even if I took a royal title, the people would never truly follow me.

sentences.zh: 今若推主，當從眾望。

translations.literal: If we are to choose a leader now, we ought to follow what the people desire.
translations.idiomatic: If we are to choose a leader now, we ought to follow the people's wishes.

sentences.zh: 羅川令蕭銑，梁氏之後，寬仁大度，有武皇之風。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Luochuan, Xiao Xian, is a descendant of the Liang house — magnanimous and broad-minded, with the bearing of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Luochuan, Xiao Xian, is a descendant of the Liang royal house — generous and broad-minded, with something of Emperor Wu's bearing.

sentences.zh: 吾又聞帝王膺籙，必有符命，而隋氏冠帶，盡號『起梁』，斯乃蕭家中興之兆。

translations.literal: I have also heard that when emperors receive the Mandate, there must be portents; and among Sui officials in caps and belts, all are styled "Rising Liang" — this is a sign of the Xiao family's restoration.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard that when emperors receive the Mandate, heaven sends omens — and among Sui officials, many bear the style name "Rising Liang," a sign that the Xiao house is destined to rise again.

sentences.zh: 今請以為主，不亦應天順人乎？

translations.literal: Now I ask that he be made leader — would this not accord with Heaven and follow the people's will?
translations.idiomatic: Let us make him our leader — would that not be to follow Heaven's will and the people's desire?

sentences.zh: 」眾乃遣人諭意，銑大悅，報景珍書曰：「我之本國，昔在有隋，以小事大，朝貢無闕。

translations.literal: " The multitude then sent someone to convey their intent; Xian was greatly pleased and replied to Jingzhen in a letter: "My ancestral state, in former times under the Sui, served the greater power with the lesser, and tribute and audiences were never wanting.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels then sent envoys to convey their proposal. Xian was delighted and wrote back to Jingzhen: "My ancestral kingdom, under the Sui, had served the greater power faithfully, never failing in tribute or attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 乃貪我土宇，滅我宗祊，我是以痛心疾首，無忘雪恥。

translations.literal: Yet they coveted our territory, extinguished our ancestral altars — therefore I am heart-stricken and head-wracked, never forgetting to wipe away the shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they coveted our lands and destroyed our ancestral temples — that is why I have been consumed with grief and rage, never forgetting the debt of vengeance.

sentences.zh: 今天啟公等，協我心事，若合符節，豈非上玄之意也！

translations.literal: Now Heaven has opened the way for you gentlemen to align with my heart's wish; if this matches tally and seal, is it not the intent of the Supreme Mystery!
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven has sent you to share my purpose — if our aims truly match, is this not the will of Heaven itself!

sentences.zh: 吾當糾率士庶，敬從來請。

translations.literal: I shall gather and lead the gentry and commoners and respectfully follow your invitation.
translations.idiomatic: I shall rally the gentry and common people and respectfully accept your invitation.

sentences.zh: 」即日集得數千人，揚言討賊而實欲相應。

translations.literal: " That same day he assembled several thousand men, proclaiming that he would punish bandits while in fact intending to join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he mustered several thousand men, publicly vowing to suppress bandits while in truth preparing to join the uprising.

sentences.zh: 遇潁川賊帥沈柳生來寇羅川縣，銑擊之，不利，因謂其眾曰：「岳州豪傑首謀起義，請我為主。

translations.literal: He encountered the Yingchuan bandit chief Shen Liusheng coming to raid Luochuan County; Xian attacked him but fared poorly, and therefore said to his followers: "The heroes of Yuezhou were first to plot the uprising and have asked me to be their leader.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yingchuan bandit chief Shen Liusheng raided Luochuan County, Xian attacked him but was defeated. He then told his followers, "The heroes of Yuezhou were the first to rise in rebellion and have asked me to lead them.

sentences.zh: 今隋政不行，天下皆叛，吾雖欲獨守，力不自全。

translations.literal: Now Sui government does not function and all under Heaven rebels; though I wish to hold out alone, my strength cannot preserve me.
translations.idiomatic: Sui rule has collapsed and the whole realm is in revolt; even if I wished to stand alone, I lack the strength to survive.

sentences.zh: 且吾先人昔都此地，若從其請，必復梁祚，遣召柳生，亦當從我。

translations.literal: Moreover, my forebears once made this place their capital; if I follow their request, the Liang throne will surely be restored — send to summon Liusheng, and he too ought to follow me.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, my ancestors once ruled from this region; if I accept their invitation, the Liang dynasty may rise again. Summon Liusheng — he will follow me as well.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆大悅，即日自稱梁公，改隋服色，建梁旗幟。

translations.literal: " The multitude was greatly pleased; that same day he styled himself Duke of Liang, changed from Sui dress and colors, and raised Liang banners.
translations.idiomatic: " His followers rejoiced. That same day he proclaimed himself Duke of Liang, cast off Sui regalia, and raised the banners of Liang.

sentences.zh: 柳生以眾歸之，拜為車騎大將軍，率眾往巴陵。

translations.literal: Liusheng brought his forces to submit; Xian appointed him General of Chariots and Cavalry and led the army toward Baling.
translations.idiomatic: Liusheng submitted with his troops and was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry; Xian then marched toward Baling at the head of his forces.

sentences.zh: 自起軍五日，遠近投附者數萬人。

translations.literal: From the raising of the army, within five days those who came to join from near and far numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within five days of raising his army, tens of thousands from near and far had flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 景珍遣徐德基、郭華率州中首領數百人詣軍迎謁，未及見銑，而前造柳生。

translations.literal: Jingzhen sent Xu Diji and Guo Hua leading several hundred leaders of the prefecture to the army to welcome and pay respects; before they could see Xian, they went ahead to Liusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen sent Xu Diji and Guo Hua with several hundred local leaders to welcome the army, but before they could reach Xian they went ahead to Liusheng's camp.

sentences.zh: 柳生謂其下曰：「我先奉梁公，勳居第一。

translations.literal: Liusheng said to his subordinates: "I was first to support the Duke of Liang, and my merit ranks first.
translations.idiomatic: Liusheng told his men, "I was the first to rally to the Duke of Liang, and my merit ranks first among you all.

sentences.zh: 今岳州兵眾，位多於我，我若入城，便出其下。

translations.literal: Now the Yuezhou troops are numerous and hold more positions than I; if I enter the city, I will be beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuezhou forces are numerous and hold higher rank than I; if I enter the city, I will be subordinate to them.

sentences.zh: 不如殺德基，質其首領，獨挾梁王進取州城。

translations.literal: Better to kill Diji, take the leaders hostage, and alone holding the King of Liang seize the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Better to kill Diji, take the other leaders hostage, and march on the prefectural city with the King of Liang under our sole control.

sentences.zh: 」遂與左右殺德基，方詣中軍白銑。

translations.literal: " He then with his attendants killed Diji and only afterward went to the central army to report to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " He and his men then killed Diji and only afterward went to headquarters to inform Xian.

sentences.zh: 銑大驚曰：「今欲撥亂，忽自相殺，我不能為汝主矣。

translations.literal: Xian was greatly alarmed and said: "We now wish to set the realm in order, yet suddenly we slaughter one another — I cannot be your leader any longer.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was appalled. "We mean to restore order to the realm," he said, "yet you turn on one another — I can no longer be your leader.

sentences.zh: 」乃步出軍門。

translations.literal: " He then walked out of the army gate on foot.
translations.idiomatic: " He walked out of the camp gate on foot.

sentences.zh: 柳生大懼，伏地請罪，銑責而赦之，令復舊位。

translations.literal: Liusheng was greatly afraid, prostrated himself to beg pardon; Xian rebuked but pardoned him and ordered him restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Liusheng prostrated himself to beg forgiveness. Xian rebuked him but pardoned him and restored him to his former command.

sentences.zh: 銑陳兵入城，景珍進言於銑曰：「徐德基丹誠奉主，柳生凶悖擅殺之，若不加誅，何以為政？

translations.literal: Xian arrayed his troops and entered the city; Jingzhen advanced counsel to Xian: "Xu Diji served his lord with red-hearted loyalty; Liusheng was vicious and rebellious and killed him on his own authority — if he is not punished, how can government be conducted?
translations.idiomatic: Xian marched into the city at the head of his troops. Jingzhen urged him: "Xu Diji served you with absolute loyalty, yet Liusheng murdered him on his own authority. If such a man goes unpunished, how can you govern?

sentences.zh: 且其為賊，凶頑已久，今雖從義，不革此心，同處一城，必將為變。

translations.literal: Moreover, as a bandit he has long been fierce and stubborn; though he now follows the righteous cause, he has not changed this heart — dwelling in one city together, he will surely bring trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, he has been a bandit chief for years — vicious and intractable. Though he now claims to follow the righteous cause, his nature has not changed. If he remains in the same city, he will surely make trouble.

sentences.zh: 若不預圖，後悔無及。

translations.literal: If we do not plan ahead, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act preemptively, we will regret it when it is too late.

sentences.zh: 」銑又從之。

translations.literal: " Xian again followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Xian again took his advice.

sentences.zh: 景珍遂斬柳生於城內。

translations.literal: Jingzhen then beheaded Liusheng within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen then had Liusheng beheaded inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 其下將帥皆潰散。

translations.literal: His subordinate generals all scattered in rout.
translations.idiomatic: His officers and troops scattered in disarray.

sentences.zh: 銑於是築壇於城南，燔燎告天，自稱梁王。

translations.literal: Xian thereupon built an altar south of the city, burned offerings and reported to Heaven, and styled himself King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then built an altar south of the city, offered burnt sacrifices to Heaven, and proclaimed himself King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 以有異鳥之瑞，建元為鳳鳴。

translations.literal: Because there was an omen of a strange bird, he established the era name Fengming (Phoenix Cry).
translations.idiomatic: Because of an omen involving a strange bird, he adopted the era name Fengming (Phoenix Cry).

sentences.zh: 義寧二年，僭稱皇帝，署置百官，一准梁故事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining, he presumptuously styled himself emperor, appointed all officials, and followed Liang precedents throughout.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yining, he declared himself emperor, appointed a full bureaucracy, and modeled his court on Liang precedent.

sentences.zh: 偽謚其從父琮為孝靖帝，祖岩為河間忠烈王，父璇為文憲王。

translations.literal: He gave posthumous titles in his false regime: his father's cousin Cong as Emperor Xiaojing, his grandfather Yan as Loyal and Fierce King of Hejian, his father Xuan as Cultured and Exemplary King.
translations.idiomatic: He conferred posthumous titles within his rebel regime: his father's cousin Cong as Emperor Xiaojing, his grandfather Yan as Loyal and Fierce King of Hejian, and his father Xuan as Cultured and Exemplary King.

sentences.zh: 封董景珍為晉王，雷世猛為秦王，鄭文秀為楚王，許玄徹為燕王，萬瓚為魯王，張繡為齊王，楊道生為宋王。

translations.literal: He enfeoffed Dong Jingzhen as King of Jin, Lei Shimeng as King of Qin, Zheng Wenxiu as King of Chu, Xu Xuanzhe as King of Yan, Wan Chan as King of Lu, Zhang Xiu as King of Qi, and Yang Daosheng as King of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Dong Jingzhen as King of Jin, Lei Shimeng as King of Qin, Zheng Wenxiu as King of Chu, Xu Xuanzhe as King of Yan, Wan Chan as King of Lu, Zhang Xiu as King of Qi, and Yang Daosheng as King of Song.

sentences.zh: 隋將張鎮州、王仁壽擊之，不能克。

translations.literal: The Sui generals Zhang Zhenzhou and Wang Renshou attacked him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui generals Zhang Zhenzhou and Wang Renshou attacked him but could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 及聞隋滅，鎮州因與寧長真等率嶺表諸州盡降於銑。

translations.literal: When they heard that Sui had perished, Zhenzhou together with Ning Changzhen and others led all the prefectures south of the ranges to surrender completely to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Sui had fallen, Zhenzhou joined Ning Changzhen and others in bringing all the Lingnan prefectures over to Xian's side.

sentences.zh: 九江鄱陽，初有林士弘僭號，俄自相誅滅，士弘逃於安成之山洞，其郡亦降於銑。

translations.literal: At Jiujiang and Poyang, at first Lin Shihong presumptuously took a title; soon they slaughtered one another, Shihong fled to a mountain cave in Ancheng, and that commandery too surrendered to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiujiang and Poyang, Lin Shihong had first declared himself a rival ruler, but his followers soon turned on one another. Shihong fled to a mountain cave in Ancheng, and the region submitted to Xian as well.

sentences.zh: 遣其將楊道生攻陷南郡，張繡略定嶺表，東至三硤，南盡交址，北拒漢川，皆附之，勝兵四十餘萬。

translations.literal: He sent his general Yang Daosheng to attack and seize Nan commandery; Zhang Xiu pacified the region south of the ranges — east to the Three Gorges, south to Jiaozhi, north to the Han River — all submitted to him; his effective troops exceeded four hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yang Daosheng to capture Nan commandery and Zhang Xiu to pacify Lingnan. His domain stretched east to the Three Gorges, south to Jiaozhi, and north to the Han River — all submitted to him, and his effective forces exceeded four hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，遷都江陵，修復園廟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he moved his capital to Jiangling and restored the imperial park temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, he moved his capital to Jiangling and restored the imperial ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 引岑文本為中書侍郎，令掌機密。

translations.literal: He brought in Cen Wuben as Vice Director of the Secretariat and ordered him to manage confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Cen Wuben Vice Director of the Secretariat and entrusted him with confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 銑又遣楊道生攻硤州，刺史許紹出兵擊破之，赴水死者大半。

translations.literal: Xian again sent Yang Daosheng to attack Xiazhou; the prefect Xu Shao led troops out, defeated him, and more than half drowned fleeing into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Xian again sent Yang Daosheng against Xiazhou, but Prefect Xu Shao marched out and routed him — more than half his men drowned trying to escape across the water.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔夔州總管趙郡王孝恭率兵討之，拔其通、開二州，斬偽東平郡王蕭阇提。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the Kuizhou area commander Prince Xiaogong of Zhao to lead troops to attack him; he captured Tong and Kai prefectures and beheaded the false Dongping Prince Xiao Sheti.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered Prince Xiaogong of Zhao, area commander of Kuizhou, to campaign against him. Xiaogong captured Tong and Kai prefectures and beheaded Xian's puppet Dongping Prince, Xiao Sheti.

sentences.zh: 時諸將橫恣，多專殺戮，銑因令罷兵，陽言營農，實奪將帥之權也。

translations.literal: At that time the generals were overbearing and willful, often killing on their own authority; Xian therefore ordered the armies disbanded, outwardly speaking of farming the fields, but in fact stripping the generals of power.
translations.idiomatic: His generals had grown arrogant and willful, often killing at will. Xian therefore ordered the armies disbanded, publicly citing the need to return to farming, but in truth to strip his commanders of military power.

sentences.zh: 其大司馬董景珍之弟為偽將軍，怨銑放其兵，遂謀為亂，事洩，為銑所誅。

translations.literal: His Grand Marshal Dong Jingzhen's younger brother, a false-regime general, resented Xian for disbanding his troops and therefore plotted rebellion; the affair leaked out and he was executed by Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jingzhen's younger brother, a general in Xian's regime, resented having his troops disbanded and plotted rebellion. When the plot was exposed, Xian had him executed.

sentences.zh: 時景珍出鎮長沙，銑下書赦之，召還江陵，景珍懼，遣間使詣孝恭送款。

translations.literal: At that time Jingzhen was garrisoned at Changsha; Xian issued a pardon in writing and summoned him back to Jiangling; Jingzhen was afraid and sent a secret envoy to Xiaogong to offer submission.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen was then stationed at Changsha. Xian issued a pardon and summoned him back to Jiangling. Fearful, Jingzhen sent a secret envoy to Xiaogong to offer his surrender.

sentences.zh: 銑遣其齊王張繡攻之，景珍謂繡曰：「『前年醢彭越，往年殺韓信』，卿豈不見之乎？

translations.literal: Xian sent his King of Qi Zhang Xiu to attack him; Jingzhen said to Xiu: "'The year before last Peng Yue was made into mincemeat; last year Han Xin was killed' — have you not seen this?
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent his King of Qi, Zhang Xiu, to attack him. Jingzhen told Zhang Xiu, "'The year before last they made Peng Yue into mincemeat; last year they killed Han Xin' — have you not seen how this ends?

sentences.zh: 奈何今日相攻！

translations.literal: Why must we attack each other today!
translations.idiomatic: Why must you attack me today!

sentences.zh: 」繡不答，進兵圍之。

translations.literal: " Xiu did not reply and advanced his troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Xiu made no reply and pressed the siege.

sentences.zh: 景珍潰圍而走，為其麾下所殺。

translations.literal: Jingzhen broke through the encirclement and fled but was killed by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhen broke out of the encirclement and fled, but his own men killed him.

sentences.zh: 銑以繡為尚書令，繡恃勳驕慢，專恣弄權，銑又惡而殺之。

translations.literal: Xian made Xiu Director of the Department of State Affairs; Xiu relied on his merit, was arrogant and insolent, and wielded power willfully on his own; Xian again detested him and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xian appointed Zhang Xiu Director of the Department of State Affairs, but Zhang Xiu, arrogant on account of his merit, abused his power. Xian came to loathe him and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 既大臣相次誅戮，故人邊將皆疑懼，多有叛者，銑不能復製，以故兵勢益弱。

translations.literal: Once the great ministers were executed one after another, old associates and frontier generals all grew suspicious and fearful; many rebelled; Xian could no longer control them — therefore his military strength grew ever weaker.
translations.idiomatic: With his chief ministers executed one after another, his old comrades and frontier generals grew fearful and suspicious. Many rebelled, and Xian could no longer control them — his military strength steadily declined.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖命趙郡王孝恭及李靖率巴蜀兵發自夔州，沿流而下；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Gaozu ordered Prince Xiaogong of Zhao and Li Jing to lead Ba-Shu troops from Kuizhou, descending along the river;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Emperor Gaozu ordered Prince Xiaogong of Zhao and Li Jing to lead Ba-Shu troops from Kuizhou downstream along the Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 廬江王瑗從襄州道，黔州刺史田世康趣辰州道，黃州總管周法明趣夏口道以圖銑。

translations.literal: Prince Yuan of Lujiang advanced by the Xiangzhou route; Qianzhou prefect Tian Shikang pressed by the Chenzhou route; Huangzhou area commander Zhou Faming pressed by the Xiakou route to converge on Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan of Lujiang advanced from Xiangzhou, Qianzhou Prefect Tian Shikang pressed in from Chenzhou, and Huangzhou area commander Zhou Faming moved on Xiakou — all converging on Xian.

sentences.zh: 及大軍將至，銑江州總管蓋彥舉以五州降。

translations.literal: When the great army was about to arrive, Xian's Jiangzhou area commander Gai Yanju surrendered with five prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: As the Tang armies approached, Xian's Jiangzhou area commander Gai Yanju surrendered with five prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將文士弘等率兵拒戰，孝恭與李靖皆擊破之，進逼其都。

translations.literal: He again sent his generals Wen Shihong and others to lead troops to resist; Xiaogong and Li Jing both defeated them and pressed on toward his capital.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wen Shihong and other generals to resist, but Xiaogong and Li Jing defeated them and advanced on his capital.

sentences.zh: 初，銑之放兵散也，自留宿衛兵士數千人，忽聞孝恭至而倉卒追兵，並江、嶺之南，道里遼遠，未能相及。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xian had disbanded and scattered his armies, he himself retained only several thousand palace guard soldiers; suddenly hearing that Xiaogong had arrived, he hastily tried to recall troops — but both south of the Yangzi and south of the ranges the roads were long and far, and they could not reach him in time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xian had disbanded his armies and kept only a few thousand palace guards. When word came that Xiaogong had arrived, he tried desperately to recall his forces — but those south of the Yangzi and beyond the Lingnan ranges were too far away to reach him in time.

sentences.zh: 孝恭縱兵入郭，布長圍以守之。

translations.literal: Xiaogong loosed his troops into the outer city and laid a long encirclement to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogong stormed the outer city and laid siege with a tight encirclement.

sentences.zh: 數日，克其水城，獲其舟船數千艘。

translations.literal: Within days they captured his water city and seized several thousand of his boats.
translations.idiomatic: Within days they captured his river fortress and seized several thousand of his vessels.

sentences.zh: 其交州總管丘和、長史高士廉、司馬杜之松等先來謁銑，聞兵敗，便詣李靖來降。

translations.literal: His Jiaozhou area commander Qiu He, chief administrator Gao Shilian, and vice minister Du Zhisong and others had earlier come to pay respects to Xian; hearing of the military defeat, they at once went to Li Jing to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: His Jiaozhou area commander Qiu He, chief administrator Gao Shilian, and vice minister Du Zhisong had earlier come to pay court to Xian; when they heard of his defeat, they went straight to Li Jing and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 銑自度救兵不至，謂其群下曰：「天不祚梁，數歸於滅。

translations.literal: Xian judged for himself that relief troops would not arrive and said to his assembled followers: "Heaven does not bless Liang; the mandate returns to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that relief would not come, Xian told his followers, "Heaven no longer favors Liang; our fate is sealed.

sentences.zh: 若待力屈，必害黎元，豈以我一人致傷百姓？

translations.literal: If we wait until strength is exhausted, we will surely harm the black-haired people — how could I alone bring injury to the common folk?
translations.idiomatic: If we hold out until our strength fails, the common people will suffer — shall I alone bring ruin upon them?

sentences.zh: 及城未拔，宜先出降，冀免亂兵，幸全眾庶。

translations.literal: Before the city is taken, we ought first to go out and surrender, hoping to spare disorder among the troops and by good fortune preserve the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Before the city falls, I ought to surrender first, in hope of sparing the people from the ravages of battle.

sentences.zh: 諸人失我，何患無君？

translations.literal: You gentlemen lose me — what worry is there of lacking a lord?
translations.idiomatic: You will lose me — but you will find another lord easily enough.

sentences.zh: 」乃巡城號令，守陴者皆慟哭。

translations.literal: " He then made the rounds of the city issuing orders; those defending the battlements all wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: " He then walked the walls giving his orders, and the defenders on the battlements wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 銑以太牢告於其廟，率官屬緦縗布幘而詣軍門，曰：「當死者唯銑，百姓非有罪也，請無殺掠。

translations.literal: Xian with the great offering reported to his ancestral temple, led his officials in coarse hemp mourning dress and cloth headbands to the army gate, and said: "The one who ought to die is only Xian; the common people are not guilty — I beg that there be no killing or plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Xian offered the great sacrifice at his ancestral temple, then led his officials to the enemy camp in mourning dress and cloth headbands. "Only I deserve to die," he said; "the people are innocent. I beg you not to slaughter or plunder them.

sentences.zh: 」孝恭囚之，送於京師。

translations.literal: " Xiaogong imprisoned him and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiaogong took him prisoner and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 銑降後數日，江南救兵十餘萬一時大至，知銑降，皆送款於孝恭。

translations.literal: Several days after Xian's surrender, more than a hundred thousand relief troops from south of the Yangzi arrived all at once; learning that Xian had surrendered, they all offered submission to Xiaogong.
translations.idiomatic: A few days after Xian surrendered, more than a hundred thousand relief troops from south of the Yangzi arrived at once. Learning of his surrender, they all submitted to Xiaogong.

sentences.zh: 銑至，高祖數其罪，銑對曰：「隋失其鹿，英雄競逐，銑無天命，故至於此。

translations.literal: When Xian arrived, Emperor Gaozu recounted his crimes; Xian replied: "Sui lost the deer in the hunt and heroes competed in pursuit; Xian lacked Heaven's mandate — therefore it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian arrived at court, Emperor Gaozu recounted his crimes. Xian replied, "When Sui lost the realm, heroes contended for it. I lacked Heaven's mandate — that is why it has come to this.

sentences.zh: 亦猶田橫南面，非負漢朝。

translations.literal: It is also like Tian Heng facing south — not a betrayal of Han.
translations.idiomatic: It is like Tian Heng claiming kingship — not a betrayal of Han.

sentences.zh: 若以為罪，甘從鼎鑊。

translations.literal: If this is held a crime, I gladly submit to the cauldron and boiling.
translations.idiomatic: If you deem that a crime, I gladly accept death in the cauldron.

sentences.zh: 」竟斬於都市，年三十九。

translations.literal: " In the end he was beheaded in the market city; he was thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he was beheaded in the capital marketplace. He was thirty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 銑自初起，五年而滅。

translations.literal: From Xian's first rising, five years until extinction.
translations.idiomatic: From his first rising to his fall, Xian's regime lasted five years.

sentences.zh: 杜伏威杜伏威，齊州章丘人也。

translations.literal: Du Fuwei — Du Fuwei was a native of Zhangqiu in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei was a native of Zhangqiu in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 少落拓，不治產業，家貧無以自給，每穿窬為盜。

translations.literal: In youth he was unrestrained, did not manage property; the family was poor and could not support itself — he constantly broke in through walls to steal.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was wild and shiftless, never managing the family estate. Poor and unable to support himself, he made his living as a burglar.

sentences.zh: 與輔公祏為刎頸之交。

translations.literal: He and Fu Gongshi were friends bound by the throat-cutting oath.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fu Gongshi were sworn brothers, bound by an oath unto death.

sentences.zh: 公祏姑家以牧羊為業，公祏數攘羊以饋之，姑有憾焉，因發其盜事。

translations.literal: Gongshi's aunt's family made their living herding sheep; Gongshi repeatedly stole sheep to give to Fuwei; the aunt bore resentment and therefore reported his thieving.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi's aunt's family raised sheep for a living. Gongshi repeatedly stole sheep to give to Fuwei. His aunt, resentful, reported his thefts to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 郡縣捕之急，伏威與公祏遂俱亡命，聚眾為群盜，時年十六。

translations.literal: The commandery and county pursued them urgently; Fuwei and Gongshi then both fled as outlaws, gathered a multitude and became bandits — he was sixteen years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities pursued them hotly, and Fuwei and Gongshi fled together, gathering followers into a bandit band. Fuwei was sixteen at the time.

sentences.zh: 常營護諸盜，出則居前，入則殿後，故其黨咸服之，共推為主。

translations.literal: He constantly protected the bandits on patrol — going out he took the fore, entering he brought up the rear — therefore his band all submitted to him and jointly made him their leader.
translations.idiomatic: He always guarded his fellow bandits on raids — marching out he took the lead, returning he brought up the rear. His comrades all respected him and chose him as their leader.

sentences.zh: 大業九年，率眾入長白山，投賊帥左君行，不被禮，因捨去，轉掠淮南，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daye he led his followers into Mount Changbai, submitted to the bandit chief Zuo Junxing, was not treated with courtesy, and therefore left; turned to plundering Huainan and styled himself general.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daye he led his followers to Mount Changbai and joined the bandit chief Zuo Junxing, but Junxing treated him poorly, so he left. He then turned to raiding Huainan and styled himself General.

sentences.zh: 時下邳有苗海潮，亦聚眾為盜，伏威使公祏謂曰：「今同苦隋政，各興大義，力分勢弱，常恐見擒，何不合以為強，則不患隋軍相制。

translations.literal: At that time at Xiapi there was Miao Haichao, who also gathered a multitude as bandits; Fuwei sent Gongshi to say to him: "We now alike suffer under Sui government, each raising a great cause — strength divided, momentum weak, constantly fearing capture — why not unite to become strong, then we need not fear Sui armies restraining us.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiapi, Miao Haichao had also raised a bandit band. Fuwei sent Fu Gongshi to tell him, "We alike suffer under Sui rule and have each raised the banner of rebellion. Divided, we are weak and easily captured. Why not unite our forces? Together we need not fear the Sui armies.

sentences.zh: 若公能為主，吾當敬從，自揆不堪，可來聽命，不則一戰以決雄雌。

translations.literal: If you, sir, can be leader, I shall respectfully follow; judging myself unfit, you may come and take command — otherwise let one battle decide who is superior.
translations.idiomatic: If you can lead, I will follow you gladly. If I am unworthy, come take command yourself — otherwise let battle decide between us.

sentences.zh: 」海潮懼，即以其眾歸於伏威。

translations.literal: " Haichao was afraid and at once brought his followers to submit to Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: " Haichao was frightened and submitted with all his followers.

sentences.zh: 江都留守遣校尉宋顥率兵討之，伏威與戰，陽為奔北，引入葭蘆中，而從上風縱火，迫其步騎陷於大澤，火至皆燒死。

translations.literal: The Jiangdu garrison commissioner sent Commandant Song Hao to lead troops against him; Fuwei gave battle, feigning a northward rout, luring them into the reed marshes, then from upwind set fire; forcing their infantry and cavalry into the great swamp, when the fire reached them all were burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdu garrison commissioner sent Commandant Song Hao against him. Fuwei feigned retreat, luring Song's men into the reed marshes, then set fire from upwind. Trapped in the swamp, Song's infantry and cavalry were burned alive.

sentences.zh: 有海陵賊帥趙破陣，聞伏威兵少而輕之，遣使召伏威，請與併力。

translations.literal: There was the Hailing bandit chief Zhao Pozhen; hearing that Fuwei's troops were few, he despised him and sent an envoy to summon Fuwei, asking to combine forces.
translations.idiomatic: The Hailing bandit chief Zhao Pozhen, hearing that Fuwei's force was small, despised him and sent an envoy inviting Fuwei to join forces.

sentences.zh: 伏威令公祏嚴兵居外以待變，親將十人持牛酒入謁。

translations.literal: Fuwei ordered Gongshi to keep the troops strict outside awaiting developments; he personally led ten men bearing oxen and wine to pay a visit.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei ordered Fu Gongshi to hold the troops ready outside while he himself led ten men bearing oxen and wine to Zhao's camp.

sentences.zh: 破陣大悅，引伏威入幕，盡集其酋帥縱酒高會。

translations.literal: Pozhen was greatly pleased, led Fuwei into his tent, gathered all his chieftains and set wine flowing in a grand feast.
translations.idiomatic: Pozhen was delighted, brought Fuwei into his tent, gathered all his chieftains, and held a grand feast.

sentences.zh: 伏威於坐斬破陣而並其眾。

translations.literal: Fuwei at the feast beheaded Pozhen and absorbed his followers.
translations.idiomatic: At the feast Fuwei struck off Pozhen's head and absorbed his entire band.

sentences.zh: 由此兵威稍盛，復屠安宜。

translations.literal: From this his military prestige grew somewhat; he again slaughtered the population of Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: His military prestige grew thereafter, and he again put Anyi to the sword.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣右御衛將軍陳棱以精兵八千討之，棱不敢戰，伏威遺棱婦人之服以激怒之，並致書號為「陳姥」，棱大怒，悉兵而至。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent Right Imperial Guard General Chen Ling with eight thousand elite troops to attack him; Ling did not dare give battle; Fuwei sent Ling women's garments to provoke him, and also sent a letter addressing him as "Old Dame Chen"; Ling was greatly enraged and brought all his troops forth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Right Imperial Guard General Chen Ling with eight thousand elite troops against him. Chen Ling hesitated to engage. Fuwei sent him women's clothing to provoke him and a letter addressing him as "Old Dame Chen." Enraged, Chen Ling marched out with his entire force.

sentences.zh: 伏威逆拒，自出陣前挑戰，棱部將射中其額，伏威怒，指之曰：「不殺汝，我終不拔箭。

translations.literal: Fuwei met him in resistance, himself coming before the battle line to challenge; one of Ling's subordinate generals shot him in the forehead; Fuwei was angry, pointed at him and said: "If I do not kill you, I will never pull out this arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei met him in battle and rode out to challenge him personally. One of Chen Ling's officers shot him in the forehead. Fuwei, enraged, pointed at the man and cried, "I will not pull out this arrow until I have killed you!

sentences.zh: 」遂馳之。

translations.literal: " He then galloped toward him.
translations.idiomatic: " He spurred his horse and charged.

sentences.zh: 棱部將走奔其陣，伏威因入棱陣，大呼衝擊，所向披靡，獲所射者，使其拔箭，然後斬之，攜其首復入棱軍奮擊，殺數十人。

translations.literal: Ling's subordinate general ran back to his formation; Fuwei thereupon entered Ling's formation, shouting loudly as he charged — wherever he went none could stand; he seized the one who had shot him, made him pull out the arrow, then beheaded him, carried his head and again entered Ling's army fighting fiercely, killing several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: The officer fled back to Chen Ling's lines. Fuwei plunged into the enemy formation, shouting as he charged and cutting down all before him. He seized the archer, made him pull out the arrow, then beheaded him. Carrying the head, he charged back into Chen Ling's army and killed dozens more.

sentences.zh: 棱陣大潰，僅以身免。

translations.literal: Ling's formation collapsed in great rout; he barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ling's army collapsed in rout; he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 乘勝破高郵縣，引兵據歷陽，自稱總管，分遣諸將略屬縣，所至輒下，江淮間小盜爭來附之。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he broke Gaoyou County, led his troops to hold Liyang, styled himself area commander, dispatched generals to subdue subordinate counties — wherever they went they fell at once; small bandits between the Jiang and Huai all vied to come and attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Following up his victory, he captured Gaoyou County and established himself at Liyang, proclaiming himself area commander. He sent his generals to subdue the surrounding counties, which fell one after another. Small bandits throughout the Jiang-Huai region flocked to join him.

sentences.zh: 伏威嘗選敢死之士五千人，號為「上募」，寵之甚厚，與同甘苦。

translations.literal: Fuwei once selected five thousand dare-to-die warriors, styled them "Elite Recruitment," favored them very generously, and shared bitter and sweet with them.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei once selected five thousand dare-to-die warriors, called them the Elite Recruitment, treated them with exceptional favor, and shared their hardships.

sentences.zh: 有攻戰，輒令上募擊之，及戰罷閱視，有中在背，便殺之，以其退而被擊也。

translations.literal: When there was attack warfare, he always had the Elite Recruitment strike; when battle ended he inspected them — if one had a wound in the back, he killed him, because he had retreated and been struck from behind.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he always sent the Elite Recruitment to the fore. After each engagement he inspected his men, and anyone with a wound in the back was executed — proof that he had turned and fled.

sentences.zh: 所獲貲財，皆以賞軍士，有戰死者，以其妻妾殉葬，故人自為戰，所向無敵。

translations.literal: All goods and wealth seized were used to reward the soldiers; when one died in battle, his wives and concubines were buried with him — therefore men fought of their own accord, and wherever they went none could withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: All booty went to reward his soldiers. When a man fell in battle, his wives and concubines were buried with him. His men therefore fought willingly, and his army was invincible.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之反也，署為歷陽太守，伏威不受。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, he appointed Fuwei prefect of Liyang; Fuwei did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, he offered Fuwei the post of prefect of Liyang, but Fuwei refused.

sentences.zh: 又移居丹陽，進用人士，大修器械，薄賦斂，除殉葬法，其犯姦盜及官人貪濁者，無輕重皆殺之。

translations.literal: He again moved his seat to Danyang, advanced and employed men of talent, greatly repaired weapons, lightened tax levies, abolished the burial-with-the-dead law; those who committed adultery, theft, or officials who were greedy and corrupt — regardless of severity all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his base to Danyang, recruited talented men, greatly expanded his armory, lightened taxes, and abolished the practice of burying wives with the dead. Adulterers, thieves, and corrupt officials were all put to death without regard to rank.

sentences.zh: 仍上表於越王侗，侗拜伏威為東道大總管，封楚王。

translations.literal: He still submitted a memorial to Prince Yue of Tong; Tong appointed Fuwei Grand Commander of the Eastern Circuit and enfeoffed him as King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial to Prince Yue of Tong, who appointed him Grand Commander of the Eastern Circuit and enfeoffed him as King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 太宗之圍王世充，遣使招之，伏威請降。

translations.literal: When the Taizong besieged Wang Shichong, he sent envoys to summon Fuwei; Fuwei requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong besieged Wang Shichong, he sent envoys to win Fuwei over, and Fuwei offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使就拜東南道行台尚書令、江淮以南安撫大使、上柱國，封吳王，賜姓李氏，預宗正屬籍，封其子德俊為山陽公，賜帛五千段、馬三百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to appoint him on the spot as Director of the Department of State Affairs of the Southeastern Circuit Executive, Pacification Commissioner south of the Jiang and Huai, Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Prince of Wu, granted the surname Li, entered in the imperial clan registry; enfeoffed his son Dejun as Duke of Shanyang and bestowed five thousand bolts of silk and three hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys to appoint him Director of the Department of State Affairs for the Southeastern Circuit, Pacification Commissioner for the lands south of the Jiang and Huai, and Pillar of State, enfeoffing him as Prince of Wu and granting him the imperial surname Li. His name was entered in the clan registry, his son Dejun was made Duke of Shanyang, and he received five thousand bolts of silk and three hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 伏威遣其將軍陳正通、徐紹宗率兵來會。

translations.literal: Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong to lead troops to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei sent his generals Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong with troops to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，遣其將軍王雄誕討李子通於杭州，擒之以獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude he sent his general Wang Xiongdan to attack Li Zitong at Hangzhou and captured him to present as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wude he sent Wang Xiongdan against Li Zitong at Hangzhou; Wang captured him and presented him to the court.

sentences.zh: 又破汪華於歙州，盡有江東、淮南之地，南接於嶺，東至於海。

translations.literal: He again defeated Wang Hua at Shezhou and wholly possessed the lands of Jiangdong and Huainan — south connecting to the ranges, east reaching to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated Wang Hua at Shezhou and came to hold all of Jiangdong and Huainan, his domain reaching south to the Lingnan ranges and east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 尋聞太宗平劉黑闥，進攻徐圓朗，伏威懼而來朝，拜為太子太保，仍兼行台尚書令。

translations.literal: Soon hearing that the Taizong had pacified Liu Heita and was advancing against Xu Yuanlang, Fuwei in fear came to court; he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent while still holding the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs of the Executive.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Emperor Taizong had defeated Liu Heita and was campaigning against Xu Yuanlang, Fuwei, fearful, came to court. He was appointed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent while retaining his post as Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 留於京師，禮之甚厚，位在齊王元吉之上，以寵異之。

translations.literal: He was kept in the capital; they treated him with great courtesy, his rank placed above Prince Qi Yuanji, to show special favor.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in the capital, where he was treated with exceptional honor, his rank placed above Prince Qi Yuanji as a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 初，輔公祏之反也，詐稱伏威之令，以紿其眾，高祖遣趙郡王孝恭討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fu Gongshi rebelled, he falsely claimed it was on Fuwei's orders to deceive his followers; Emperor Gaozu sent Prince Xiaogong of Zhao to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, he falsely claimed to act on Fuwei's orders to deceive his followers. Emperor Gaozu sent Prince Xiaogong of Zhao against him.

sentences.zh: 時伏威在長安暴卒。

translations.literal: At that time Fuwei died suddenly in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fuwei died suddenly in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 及公祏平，孝恭收得公祏反辭，不曉其詐，遽以奏聞，乃除伏威名，籍沒其妻子。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was pacified, Xiaogong seized Gongshi's rebel documents, did not understand the deception, and hastily reported to the throne; Fuwei's name was then struck from the rolls and his wife and children confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi was defeated, Xiaogong seized his rebel correspondence. Not recognizing the deception, he reported immediately to the throne. Fuwei's name was struck from the rolls and his wife and children were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，太宗知其冤，赦之，復其官爵，葬以公禮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, the Taizong knew he had been wronged, pardoned him, restored his offices and titles, and buried him with ducal rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, Emperor Taizong learned of the injustice, posthumously pardoned him, restored his offices and titles, and buried him with ducal honors.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏輔公祏，齊州臨濟人。

translations.literal: Fu Gongshi — Fu Gongshi was a native of Linji in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi was a native of Linji in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 隋末，從杜伏威為群盜。

translations.literal: At the end of Sui he followed Du Fuwei as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui dynasty he followed Du Fuwei into banditry.

sentences.zh: 初，伏威自稱總管，以公祏為長史。

translations.literal: At first, when Fuwei styled himself area commander, he made Gongshi his chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei first proclaimed himself area commander, he appointed Gongshi his chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 李子通之敗沈法興也，伏威使公祏以精卒數千渡江討之。

translations.literal: When Li Zitong defeated Shen Faxing, Fuwei sent Gongshi with several thousand elite troops across the river to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zitong defeated Shen Faxing, Fuwei sent Gongshi with several thousand elite troops across the Yangzi to attack Li.

sentences.zh: 子通率眾數萬以拒公祏，兵鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: Zitong led tens of thousands to resist Gongshi; his military edge was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong led tens of thousands to resist Gongshi, and his army fought with great ferocity.

sentences.zh: 公祏簡甲士千人，皆使執長刀，仍令千餘人隨後，令之曰：「有卻者斬。

translations.literal: Gongshi selected a thousand armored warriors, all made to wield long blades, and still ordered more than a thousand men to follow behind, commanding them: "Whoever retreats — behead.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi selected a thousand armored warriors armed with long blades and placed more than a thousand men behind them with the order: "Anyone who retreats will be beheaded.

sentences.zh: 」公祏自領餘眾，復居其後。

translations.literal: " Gongshi himself led the remaining troops and again took position behind them.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongshi himself led the remaining troops and took up position in the rear.

sentences.zh: 俄而子通方陣而前，公祏所遣千人皆殊死決戰，公祏乃縱左右翼攻之，子通大潰，降其眾數千人。

translations.literal: Soon Zitong had just formed his battle line and advanced; the thousand men Gongshi sent all fought to the death; Gongshi then loosed his left and right wings to attack — Zitong collapsed in great rout, and several thousand of his followers surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zitong advanced in battle formation, Gongshi's thousand front-line warriors fought to the death. Gongshi then unleashed his flanking forces, routing Li Zitong completely and accepting the surrender of several thousand of his men.

sentences.zh: 公祏尋與伏威遣使歸國，拜為淮南道行台尚書左僕射，封舒國公。

translations.literal: Gongshi soon together with Fuwei sent envoys to submit to the state; he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs of the Huainan Circuit Executive and enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi soon joined Fuwei in sending envoys to submit to the Tang court. He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs for the Huainan Circuit and enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，伏威與公祏少相愛狎，公祏年長，伏威每兄事之，軍中咸呼為伯，畏敬與伏威等。

translations.literal: At first Fuwei and Gongshi in youth were mutually affectionate and familiar; Gongshi was older, and Fuwei always treated him as an elder brother — in the army all called him Elder Uncle, fearing and respecting him equally with Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: In their youth Fuwei and Gongshi had been close friends. Gongshi was the elder, and Fuwei always treated him as an elder brother. The army called him Elder Uncle and respected him as they did Fuwei himself.

sentences.zh: 伏威潛忌之，為署其養子闞棱為左將軍，王雄誕為右將軍，推公祏為僕射，外示尊崇，而陰奪其兵權。

translations.literal: Fuwei secretly resented him; he appointed his foster son Kan Ling as Left General and Wang Xiongdan as Right General, promoted Gongshi to Vice Director — outwardly showing honor while secretly stripping him of military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei secretly grew jealous of him. He appointed his foster son Kan Ling as Left General and Wang Xiongdan as Right General, while promoting Gongshi to Vice Director — outwardly honoring him but secretly stripping him of military power.

sentences.zh: 公祏知其意，怏怏不平，乃與故人左遊仙偽學道辟榖以遠其事。

translations.literal: Gongshi knew his intent and was resentful and discontent; he therefore with his old friend Zuo Youxian feigned studying the Way and grain avoidance to distance himself from affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi understood his intent and grew resentful. He and his old friend Zuo Youxian pretended to study the Way and practice grain avoidance to distance themselves from court affairs.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，伏威將入朝，留公祏居守，復令雄誕典兵以副公祏，陰謂曰：「吾入京，若不失職，無令公祏為變。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude, when Fuwei was about to enter court, he left Gongshi to hold the garrison, again ordered Xiongdan to manage troops to assist Gongshi, and secretly told him: "When I enter the capital, if I do not lose my post, do not let Gongshi make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude, as Fuwei prepared to go to court, he left Gongshi in charge of Jiangnan and ordered Wang Xiongdan to assist him with the troops. He told Xiongdan privately, "If I retain my position in the capital, do not let Gongshi rebel.

sentences.zh: 」其後左遊仙乃說公祏令反。

translations.literal: " Afterward Zuo Youxian then urged Gongshi to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuo Youxian then persuaded Gongshi to rebel.

sentences.zh: 會雄誕屬疾於家，公祏奪其兵，詐言伏威不得還江南，貽書令其起兵。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiongdan was ill at home; Gongshi seized his troops, falsely claimed Fuwei could not return to Jiangnan, and sent letters ordering them to raise the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xiongdan fell ill at home, Gongshi seized his troops, falsely claimed that Fuwei could not return to Jiangnan, and sent orders for the army to rise in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 因僭即偽位，自稱宋國，於陳故都築宮以居焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon presumptuously assumed the false throne, styled himself State of Song, and built a palace at the former Chen capital to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: He then presumptuously declared himself emperor of a State of Song and built a palace at the former Chen capital to serve as his residence.

sentences.zh: 署置百官，以左遊仙為兵部尚書、東南道大使、越州總管。

translations.literal: He appointed all officials, making Zuo Youxian Minister of War, Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit, and area commander of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed a full bureaucracy, making Zuo Youxian Minister of War, Commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit, and area commander of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 大修兵甲，轉漕糧饋。

translations.literal: He greatly repaired armor and weapons and transported grain by canal for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly expanded his armaments and organized grain transport by canal.

sentences.zh: 時吳興賊帥沈法興據毗陵，公祏擊破之。

translations.literal: At that time the Wuxing bandit chief Shen Faxing held Piling; Gongshi attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing bandit chief Shen Faxing held Piling at the time; Gongshi attacked and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 又遣其將馮惠亮屯於博望山，陳正通、徐紹宗屯於青林山以拒官軍。

translations.literal: He again sent his general Feng Huiliang to encamp at Mount Bowang, Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong to encamp at Mount Qinglin to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Feng Huiliang to hold Mount Bowang and Chen Zhengtong and Xu Shaozong to hold Mount Qinglin against the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 高祖命趙郡王孝恭率諸將奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Prince Xiaogong of Zhao to lead the generals in fierce attack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu ordered Prince Xiaogong of Zhao to lead the generals in a fierce assault and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 紹宗、正通以五騎奔於丹陽。

translations.literal: Shaozong and Zhengtong fled to Danyang with five horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong and Zhengtong fled to Danyang with only five horsemen.

sentences.zh: 公祏懼而遁走，欲就左遊仙於會稽，至武康，為野人所執，送於丹陽，孝恭斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Gongshi in fear fled, wishing to join Zuo Youxian at Kuaiji; reaching Wukang he was seized by country folk, sent to Danyang; Xiaogong beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Gongshi fled toward Kuaiji to join Zuo Youxian. At Wukang he was seized by local villagers and sent to Danyang, where Xiaogong beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 公祏與伏威同起，至滅凡十三載，江東悉平。

translations.literal: Gongshi rose together with Fuwei; from rise to extinction altogether thirteen years — Jiangdong was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi had risen with Fuwei; from their first rising to his fall thirteen years passed, and Jiangdong was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 初，伏威養壯士三十餘人為假子，分領兵馬，唯闞棱、王雄誕知名。

translations.literal: At first Fuwei raised more than thirty stalwart men as foster sons, each commanding troops and horses — only Kan Ling and Wang Xiongdan were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei had taken more than thirty stalwart warriors as foster sons, each commanding troops; only Kan Ling and Wang Xiongdan were widely known.

sentences.zh: 闞棱闞棱，齊州臨濟人。

translations.literal: Kan Ling — Kan Ling was a native of Linji in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ling was a native of Linji in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 善用大刀，長一丈，施兩刃，名為陌刃，每一舉，輒斃數人，前無當者。

translations.literal: He excelled at using the great blade — ten feet long, fitted with two edges, called the street blade; with each swing several men fell dead; none could stand before him.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled with a great blade ten feet long, double-edged, called the street blade. With each swing several men fell, and none could stand before him.

sentences.zh: 及伏威據有江淮之地，棱數有戰功，署為左將軍。

translations.literal: When Fuwei held the lands of the Jiang and Huai, Ling had repeated battle merit and was appointed Left General.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei held the Jiang-Huai region, Ling won repeated victories and was appointed Left General.

sentences.zh: 伏威步兵皆出自群賊，類多放縱，有相侵奪者，棱必殺之，雖親故無所舍，令行禁止，路不拾遺。

translations.literal: Fuwei's infantry all came from bandit groups and were mostly undisciplined; when some robbed one another, Ling always killed them — even kin and old friends he did not spare; orders were enforced and forbidden things halted — no one picked up lost objects on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei's infantry, drawn from bandit ranks, were largely undisciplined. Ling executed anyone who robbed his fellows, sparing neither kin nor friends. His discipline was so strict that lost objects lay untouched on the roads.

sentences.zh: 後從伏威入朝，拜左領軍將軍，遷越州都督。

translations.literal: Later he followed Fuwei to court, was appointed General of the Left Guard Army, and transferred to be area commander of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Fuwei to court, was appointed General of the Left Guard Army, and was made area commander of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 及公祏僭號，棱從軍討之，與陳正通相遇。

translations.literal: When Gongshi presumptuously took a title, Ling followed the army to attack him and encountered Chen Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi declared himself emperor, Ling joined the campaign against him and encountered Chen Zhengtong.

sentences.zh: 陣方接，棱脫兜鍪謂賊眾曰：「汝不識我邪？

translations.literal: The battle lines had just joined when Ling removed his helmet and said to the rebel host: "Do you not know me?
translations.idiomatic: As the battle lines met, Ling removed his helmet and called to the rebel troops, "Do you not know who I am?

sentences.zh: 何敢來戰！

translations.literal: How dare you come to fight!
translations.idiomatic: How dare you fight me!

sentences.zh: 」其眾多棱舊之所部，由是各無鬥志，或有還拜者。

translations.literal: " Many of their host had formerly been under Ling's command; therefore each lost fighting spirit, and some turned back to pay obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: " Many of them had once served under Ling, and they lost all will to fight; some turned and bowed to him.

sentences.zh: 公祏之破，棱功居多，頗有自矜之色。

translations.literal: In Gongshi's defeat, Ling's merit was greatest; he showed considerable self-congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: Ling's merit in defeating Gongshi was the greatest, and he grew somewhat proud.

sentences.zh: 及擒公祏，誣棱與己通謀。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was captured, he falsely accused Ling of conspiring with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi was captured, he falsely accused Ling of conspiring with him.

sentences.zh: 又杜伏威、王雄誕及棱家產在賊中者，合從原放，孝恭乃皆籍沒。

translations.literal: Moreover, the family property of Du Fuwei, Wang Xiongdan, and Ling that was in rebel hands ought jointly to have been released and restored — yet Xiaogong confiscated it all.
translations.idiomatic: The family property of Du Fuwei, Wang Xiongdan, and Ling that had fallen into rebel hands should have been restored, but Xiaogong confiscated it all.

sentences.zh: 棱訴理之，有忤於孝恭，孝恭怒，遂以謀反誅之。

translations.literal: Ling appealed for justice; this offended Xiaogong; Xiaogong in anger then executed him on a charge of plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ling appealed for justice, offending Xiaogong, who in anger had him executed on a charge of treason.

sentences.zh: 王雄誕王雄誕者，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Xiongdan — Wang Xiongdan was a native of Jiyin in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiongdan was a native of Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，伏威之起也，用其計，屢有克獲，署為驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: At first, when Fuwei rose, he used Xiongdan's plans and repeatedly achieved captures; he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei first rose, he relied on Xiongdan's counsel and won repeated victories, appointing him General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 伏威後率眾渡淮，與海陵賊李子通合。

translations.literal: Fuwei later led his followers across the Huai and joined with the Hailing bandit Li Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei later led his forces across the Huai and joined with the Hailing bandit Li Zitong.

sentences.zh: 後子通惡伏威雄武，使騎襲之，伏威被重瘡墮馬，雄誕負之，逃於葭蘆中。

translations.literal: Later Zitong resented Fuwei's martial prowess and sent cavalry to raid him; Fuwei received grave wounds and fell from his horse; Xiongdan carried him on his back and fled into the reed marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong, resenting Fuwei's martial prowess, sent cavalry to attack him. Fuwei was gravely wounded and fell from his horse; Xiongdan carried him on his back and fled into the reed marshes.

sentences.zh: 伏威復招集餘黨，攻劫郡縣，隋將來整又擊破之，亡失餘眾。

translations.literal: Fuwei again gathered remnant followers, attacked and plundered commanderies and counties; the Sui general Lai Zheng again defeated him and he lost his remaining host.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei rallied his remnant followers and raided the commanderies and counties, but the Sui general Lai Zheng defeated him again and he lost what remained of his force.

sentences.zh: 其部將西門君儀妻王氏勇決多力，負伏威而走，雄誕率麾下壯士十餘人衛護。

translations.literal: His subordinate general Ximen Junyi's wife Lady Wang was brave, resolute, and very strong — she carried Fuwei on her back as they fled; Xiongdan led more than ten stalwart warriors of his command to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: His officer Ximen Junyi's wife, Lady Wang, was brave and exceptionally strong. She carried Fuwei on her back as they fled, while Xiongdan led a dozen of his finest warriors to guard them.

sentences.zh: 隋軍追至，雄誕輒還御之，身被數槍，勇氣彌厲，竟脫伏威。

translations.literal: When Sui troops pursued, Xiongdan always turned back to hold them off; his body received several spear wounds, yet his courage grew fiercer — in the end he brought Fuwei to safety.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui troops pursued, Xiongdan always turned to fight them off. He took several spear wounds, yet fought with growing fury until Fuwei was safe.

sentences.zh: 時闞棱年長於雄誕，故軍中號棱為大將軍，雄誕為小將軍。

translations.literal: At that time Kan Ling was older than Xiongdan, so in the army Ling was called Great General and Xiongdan Little General.
translations.idiomatic: Kan Ling was older than Xiongdan, so the army called Ling the Great General and Xiongdan the Little General.

sentences.zh: 後伏威令輔公祏擊李子通於江都，使雄誕與棱為副，戰於溧水，子通大敗。

translations.literal: Later Fuwei ordered Fu Gongshi to attack Li Zitong at Jiangdu, making Xiongdan and Ling his deputies; they fought at Lishui — Zitong suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fuwei ordered Fu Gongshi to attack Li Zitong at Jiangdu, with Xiongdan and Ling as his deputies. They fought at Lishui and routed Li Zitong completely.

sentences.zh: 公祏乘勝追之，卻為子通所破，軍士皆堅壁不敢出。

translations.literal: Gongshi pressed the victory in pursuit but was in turn defeated by Zitong; the soldiers all held their walls and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshi pursued in victory but was in turn defeated by Li Zitong; his soldiers held their camps and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 雄誕謂公祏曰：「子通軍無營壘，且狃於初勝而不設備，若擊之，必克。

translations.literal: Xiongdan said to Gongshi: "Zitong's army has no fortified camps, and being accustomed to their first victory they make no preparations — if we attack, we will surely overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan told Gongshi, "Li Zitong's army has no fortified camp and, emboldened by their first victory, is unprepared. If we attack now, we are sure to win.

sentences.zh: 」公祏不從。

translations.literal: " Gongshi did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongshi refused.

sentences.zh: 雄誕以其私屬數百人銜枚夜擊之，因順風縱火，子通大敗，走渡太湖，復破沈法興，居其地。

translations.literal: Xiongdan with several hundred of his personal followers, gags in their mouths, struck by night; taking advantage of the wind he set fire — Zitong suffered great defeat, fled across Lake Tai, again defeated Shen Faxing, and occupied his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan led several hundred of his personal followers in a night attack with gags in their mouths, setting fire downwind. Li Zitong was routed and fled across Lake Tai. Xiongdan then defeated Shen Faxing and occupied his territory.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞伏威據有吳、楚，遣使諭之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu heard that Fuwei held Wu and Chu and sent envoys to instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu learned that Fuwei held Wu and Chu, he sent envoys to summon him.

sentences.zh: 雄誕率眾討之，子通以精兵守獨松嶺，雄誕遣其部將陳當率千餘人，出其不意，乘高據險，多張旗幟，夜則縛炬火於樹上，佈滿山澤間。

translations.literal: Xiongdan led his host to attack him; Zitong with elite troops held Dusong Ridge; Xiongdan sent his subordinate general Chen Dang with more than a thousand men, taking them unawares, seizing the heights and holding difficult ground, setting up many banners; at night they bound torches to trees, spreading them throughout the mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan led his forces against Li Zitong, who held Dusong Ridge with elite troops. Xiongdan sent Chen Dang with more than a thousand men to take him by surprise, seizing the high ground and planting many banners. At night they bound torches to the trees until the hills and marshes blazed with light.

sentences.zh: 子通大懼，燒營而走，保於杭州。

translations.literal: Zitong was greatly afraid, burned his camp and fled, holding out at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Li Zitong burned his camp and fled to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 雄誕追擊敗之，擒子通於陣，送於京師。

translations.literal: Xiongdan pursued, defeated him, captured Zitong on the battlefield, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan pursued, defeated him, captured Li Zitong on the field, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 歙州首領汪華，隋末據本郡稱王十餘年，雄誕回軍擊之。

translations.literal: The Shezhou chieftain Wang Hua, at the end of Sui, held his commandery and styled himself king for more than ten years; Xiongdan turned his army back to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Shezhou chieftain Wang Hua had held his commandery and styled himself king for more than ten years at the end of Sui. Xiongdan turned his army to attack him.

sentences.zh: 華出新安洞口以拒雄誕，甲兵甚銳。

translations.literal: Hua came out from the Xinan pass mouth to resist Xiongdan; his armored troops were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua marched out from the Xinan pass to resist Xiongdan with a fierce, well-armored force.

sentences.zh: 雄誕伏精兵於山谷間，率羸弱數千人當之，戰才合，偽退歸本營。

translations.literal: Xiongdan hid elite troops in the mountain valleys, led several thousand weak troops to meet them; battle had just joined when he feigned retreat back to his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan hid elite troops in the valleys and advanced with a few thousand weak troops as bait. As soon as battle was joined, he feigned retreat to his camp.

sentences.zh: 華攻之不能克，會日暮欲還，雄誕伏兵已據其洞口，華不得入，窘急面縛而降。

translations.literal: Hua attacked but could not overcome them; as evening came he wished to return — Xiongdan's ambush troops had already seized his pass mouth; Hua could not enter, in dire straits he bound his face and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hua attacked but could not break through. At dusk he tried to withdraw, but Xiongdan's ambush had already seized the pass. Unable to enter, Wang Hua bound himself and surrendered in desperation.

sentences.zh: 蘇州賊帥聞人遂安據崑山縣而無所屬，伏威又命雄誕攻之。

translations.literal: The Suzhou bandit chief Wenren Sui'an held Kunshan County and acknowledged no master; Fuwei again ordered Xiongdan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Suzhou bandit chief Wenren Sui'an held Kunshan County without acknowledging any master. Fuwei again ordered Xiongdan to attack him.

sentences.zh: 雄誕以崑山險隘，難以力勝，遂單騎詣其城下，陳國威靈，示以禍福，遂安感悅，率諸將出降。

translations.literal: Xiongdan, because Kunshan was narrow and perilous and hard to overcome by force, then rode alone to beneath his walls, set forth the state's majesty, showed fortune and misfortune — Sui'an was moved and pleased, and led his generals out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Kunshan narrow and defensible and difficult to take by force, Xiongdan rode alone to the city walls, proclaimed the imperial majesty, and showed the consequences of resistance and submission. Moved, Sui'an led his generals out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 以前後功授歙州總管，封宜春郡公。

translations.literal: For his cumulative merit before and after, he was appointed area commander of Shezhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Yichun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For his accumulated merits he was appointed area commander of Shezhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 伏威之入朝也，留輔公祏鎮江南，而兵馬屬於雄誕。

translations.literal: When Fuwei entered court, he left Fu Gongshi to garrison Jiangnan, while troops and horses were under Xiongdan's authority.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei went to court, he left Fu Gongshi to hold Jiangnan while placing the troops under Xiongdan's command.

sentences.zh: 公祏將為逆，奪其兵，拘之別室，遣西門君儀諭以反計，雄誕曰：「當今方太平，吳王又在京輦，國家威靈，無遠不被，公何得為族滅事耶！

translations.literal: When Gongshi was about to rebel, he seized Xiongdan's troops and confined him in a separate room, sent Ximen Junyi to explain the rebel plan; Xiongdan said: "The realm is now at peace, the Prince of Wu is again in the capital region, the state's majesty reaches everywhere without exception — how can you, sir, undertake an affair that exterminates your clan!
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi prepared to rebel, he seized Xiongdan's troops and confined him in a separate room, sending Ximen Junyi to urge him to join. Xiongdan said, "The realm is at peace, the Prince of Wu is at court, and imperial authority reaches to the farthest corners — how can you undertake an act that will destroy your entire clan!

sentences.zh: 雄誕有死而已，不敢聞命。

translations.literal: Xiongdan has only death — he dares not hear the command.
translations.idiomatic: I have only death to offer — I will not obey such an order.

sentences.zh: 」公祏知不可屈，遂縊殺之。

translations.literal: " Gongshi knew he could not be bent and therefore strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Knowing he could not be swayed, Gongshi had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 雄誕善撫卹將士，皆得其死力，每破城鎮，約勒部下，絲毫無犯，故死之日，江南士庶莫不為之流涕。

translations.literal: Xiongdan was skilled at comforting and caring for officers and soldiers — all gave him their utmost loyalty; whenever he captured a walled town or market, he restrained his subordinates so that not the slightest thing was violated — therefore on the day of his death, gentry and commoners of Jiangnan none failed to weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan was skilled at winning the loyalty of his officers and men, who served him unto death. Whenever he captured a town, he strictly forbade his troops from harming the populace. When he died, gentry and commoners throughout Jiangnan wept for him.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其節，命其子果襲封宜春郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu praised his integrity and ordered his son Guo to inherit the enfeoffment as Duke of Yichun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu praised his integrity and ordered his son Guo to inherit the title of Duke of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，追贈左衛大將軍、越州都督，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: When the Taizong took the throne, he posthumously awarded Left Guard General and area commander of Yuezhou, with posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he posthumously awarded him the titles of Left Guard General and area commander of Yuezhou, with the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 果，垂拱初官至廣州都督，安西大都護。

translations.literal: Guo, at the beginning of Chuigong reached the posts of area commander of Guangzhou and Grand Protector of the Pacified West.
translations.idiomatic: Guo, at the beginning of the Chuigong era, rose to area commander of Guangzhou and Grand Protector of the Pacified West.

sentences.zh: 沈法興沈法興，湖州武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Faxing — Shen Faxing was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Faxing was a native of Wukang in Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 父恪，陳特進、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Ke was a Special Advancement of Chen and prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ke had been a Special Advancement of Chen and prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 法興，隋大業末為吳興郡守。

translations.literal: Faxing, at the end of Daye under Sui, was prefect of Wuxing commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era under Sui, Faxing was prefect of Wuxing commandery.

sentences.zh: 東陽賊帥樓世干舉兵圍郡城，煬帝令法興與太僕丞元祐討之。

translations.literal: The Dongyang bandit chief Lou Shigan raised troops and besieged the commandery city; Emperor Yang ordered Faxing together with the Vice Director of the Imperial Stud Yuan You to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongyang bandit chief Lou Shigan besieged the commandery city. Emperor Yang ordered Faxing and the Vice Director of the Imperial Stud, Yuan You, to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 俄而宇文化及弒煬帝於江都，法興自以代居南土，宗族數千家，為遠近所服，乃與祐部將孫士漢、陳果仁執祐於坐，號令遠近。

translations.literal: Soon Yuwen Huaji murdered Emperor Yang at Jiangdu; Faxing considered that his family for generations had dwelt in the southern lands, his clan numbered several thousand households, and was obeyed by near and far — he therefore with You's subordinate generals Sun Shihan and Chen Guoren seized You at his seat and issued orders to near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuwen Huaji murdered Emperor Yang at Jiangdu. Faxing, whose family had lived in the south for generations and whose clan numbered thousands of households respected throughout the region, joined Yuan You's subordinate generals Sun Shihan and Chen Guoren in seizing You at a banquet and proclaiming authority over the surrounding lands.

sentences.zh: 以誅化及為名，發自東陽，行收兵，將趨江都，下餘杭郡，比至烏程，精卒六萬。

translations.literal: Under the banner of punishing Huaji, he set out from Dongyang, marched gathering troops, intending to press toward Jiangdu, subdued Yuhang commandery — by the time he reached Wucheng he had sixty thousand elite soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Marching under the banner of punishing Huaji, he set out from Dongyang, gathering troops as he went toward Jiangdu. He captured Yuhang commandery, and by the time he reached Wucheng his elite force numbered sixty thousand.

sentences.zh: 毗陵郡通守路道德率兵拒之，法興請與連和，因會盟襲殺道德，進據其城。

translations.literal: Piling commandery's communicating defender Lu Daode led troops to resist him; Faxing requested alliance; at the alliance meeting he ambushed and killed Daode and advanced to hold his city.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Daode, communicating defender of Piling commandery, led troops to resist him. Faxing proposed an alliance, then ambushed and killed Daode at the treaty meeting and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 時齊郡賊帥樂伯通據丹陽，為化及城守，法興使果仁攻陷之，於是據有江表十餘郡，自署江南道總管。

translations.literal: At that time the Qijun bandit chief Yue Botong held Danyang, garrisoning the city for Huaji; Faxing sent Guoren to attack and capture it — he thereupon held more than ten commanderies south of the Yangzi and styled himself area commander of the Jiangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Qijun bandit chief Yue Botong held Danyang in service of Huaji. Faxing sent Chen Guoren to capture it and thereby came to hold more than ten commanderies south of the Yangzi, proclaiming himself area commander of the Jiangnan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 復聞越王侗立，乃上表於侗，自稱大司馬、錄尚書事、天門公。

translations.literal: Again hearing that Prince Yue of Tong had been established, he submitted a memorial to Tong, styling himself Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Prince Yue of Tong had been enthroned, he submitted a memorial to him, styling himself Grand Marshal, Recorder of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Tianmen.

sentences.zh: 承製置百官，以陳果仁為司徒，孫士漢為司空，蔣元超為尚書左僕射，殷芊為尚書左丞，徐令言為尚書右丞，劉子翼為選部侍郎，李百藥為府掾。

translations.literal: By imperial rescript he appointed all officials: Chen Guoren as Minister of Education, Sun Shihan as Minister of Works, Jiang Yuanchao as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yin Qian as Left Assistant Director, Xu Lingyan as Right Assistant Director, Liu Ziyi as Vice Director of the Selection Bureau, Li Baiyao as bureau aide.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial rescript he appointed a full bureaucracy: Chen Guoren as Minister of Education, Sun Shihan as Minister of Works, Jiang Yuanchao as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Yin Qian as Left Assistant Director, Xu Lingyan as Right Assistant Director, Liu Ziyi as Vice Director of the Selection Bureau, and Li Baiyao as a bureau aide.

sentences.zh: 法興自克毗陵後，謂江淮已南可指捴而定，專立威刑，將士有小過，便即誅戮，而言笑自若，由是將士解體。

translations.literal: After Faxing himself captured Piling, he considered that south of the Jiang and Huai could be taken with a gesture; he exclusively established severe punishments — officers and soldiers with small faults were at once executed, yet he spoke and laughed as if at ease — therefore the officers and soldiers lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing Piling, Faxing believed the lands south of the Jiang and Huai could be taken at a gesture. He ruled through terror, executing officers and soldiers for the slightest fault while chatting and laughing as if nothing had happened. His troops lost all morale.

sentences.zh: 稱梁，建元曰延康，改易隋官，頗依陳氏故事。

translations.literal: He styled himself Liang, established the era name Yankang, changed Sui offices, largely following Chen precedents.
translations.idiomatic: He declared himself ruler of Liang, adopted the era name Yankang, reformed the Sui bureaucracy, and largely followed Chen precedent.

sentences.zh: 是時，杜伏威據歷陽，陳棱據江都，李子通據海陵，並握強兵，俱有窺覦江表之志。

translations.literal: At that time Du Fuwei held Liyang, Chen Ling held Jiangdu, Li Zitong held Hailing — all grasped strong armies and alike harbored designs to covet the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Fuwei held Liyang, Chen Ling held Jiangdu, and Li Zitong held Hailing — each commanding a powerful army and each eyeing the lands south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 法興三面受敵，軍數挫衄。

translations.literal: Faxing received enemies on three sides; his army's numbers suffered setbacks and defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing was beset on three sides, and his armies suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 陳棱尋被李子通圍於江都，棱窘急，送質求救，法興使其子綸領兵數萬救之。

translations.literal: Before long Chen Ling was besieged by Li Zitong at Jiangdu; Ling was in dire straits, sent hostages to seek rescue — Faxing sent his son Lun leading tens of thousands of troops to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen Ling was besieged at Jiangdu by Li Zitong. In desperate straits, Ling sent hostages to plead for aid, and Faxing dispatched his son Lun at the head of tens of thousands of men to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 子通率眾攻綸，大敗，乘勝渡江，陷其京口。

translations.literal: Zitong led the masses to attack Lun — great defeat; riding victory he crossed the river and captured his Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong led his army against Lun and routed him, then pressed his advantage across the river and seized Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 法興使蔣元超拒之於庱亭，元超戰死。

translations.literal: Faxing sent Jiang Yuanchao to resist him at Tingting; Yuanchao died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing sent Jiang Yuanchao to hold Tingting, but Yuanchao was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 法興與左右數百人投吳郡賊帥聞人遂安，遣其將葉孝辯迎之。

translations.literal: Faxing with several hundred attendants went over to the Wujun bandit chief Wenren Sui'an; he dispatched his general Ye Xiaobian to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing fled to the Wujun bandit chief Wenren Sui'an with several hundred followers and sent his general Ye Xiaobian to receive him.

sentences.zh: 法興至中路而悔，欲殺孝辯，更向會稽。

translations.literal: Faxing reaching mid-journey regretted it, wished to kill Xiaobian, and turned again toward Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Midway on the journey Faxing had second thoughts and plotted to kill Xiaobian, then turned toward Kuaiji instead.

sentences.zh: 孝辯覺之，法興懼，乃赴江死。

translations.literal: Xiaobian perceived it; Faxing feared — he therefore went to the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobian discovered the plot. In terror, Faxing threw himself into the river and drowned.

sentences.zh: 初，法興以義寧二年起兵，至武德三年而滅。

translations.literal: In the beginning, Faxing rose in arms in the second year of Yining — by the third year of Wude he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing had first raised troops in the second year of Yining and was destroyed by the third year of Wude.

sentences.zh: 李子通李子通，東海丞人也。

translations.literal: Li Zitong — Li Zitong was a native of Cheng in Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong was a native of Cheng in Donghai.

sentences.zh: 少貧賤，以魚獵為事。

translations.literal: In youth poor and lowly, he made fishing and hunting his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was poor and humble, making his living by fishing and hunting.

sentences.zh: 居鄉里，見班白提挈者，必代之。
