translations.literal: Dwelling in his village lane, whenever he saw white-haired ones carrying loads he always took their place.
translations.idiomatic: In his home village he would always take the burdens from any white-haired elder he saw carrying loads.

sentences.zh: 性好施惠，家無蓄積，睚眥之怨必報。

translations.literal: His nature loved granting kindness; the family had no accumulations — grudges over the smallest slights he always repaid.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature and kept nothing in store, yet he always exacted revenge for the slightest slight.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，有賊帥左才相，自號博山公，據齊郡之長白山，子通歸之，以武力為才相所重。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye under Sui there was the bandit chief Zuo Caixiang, who styled himself Duke of Boshan, holding Changbai Mountain in Qijun — Zitong went over to him and by martial prowess was valued by Caixiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era, the bandit chief Zuo Caixiang styled himself Duke of Boshan and held Changbai Mountain in Qijun. Zitong joined him and won Caixiang's esteem through his fighting prowess.

sentences.zh: 有鄉人陷於賊者，必全護之。

translations.literal: Whenever fellow-villagers fell into the bandits' hands he always fully protected them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever fellow villagers fell into the bandits' hands, he always protected them.

sentences.zh: 時諸賊皆殘忍，唯子通獨行仁恕，由是人多歸之，未半歲，兵至萬人。

translations.literal: At that time all the bandits were cruel — only Zitong alone practiced benevolence and clemency; thereby many people came over to him — before half a year troops reached ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: All the other bandit leaders were cruel, but Zitong alone practiced mercy, and many men flocked to him. Within half a year his force numbered ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 才相稍忌之，子通自引去，因渡淮，與杜伏威合。

translations.literal: Caixiang gradually grew jealous of him; Zitong himself withdrew, then crossed the Huai and joined with Du Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Caixiang grew jealous of him, and Zitong withdrew on his own initiative, crossed the Huai, and joined Du Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 尋為隋將來整所敗，子通擁其餘眾奔海陵，得眾二萬，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was defeated by the Sui general Lai Zheng; Zitong gathered the remaining masses and fled to Hailing, gaining twenty thousand followers, styling himself General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Sui general Lai Zheng defeated him. Zitong gathered the survivors and fled to Hailing, where he mustered twenty thousand men and proclaimed himself General.

sentences.zh: 初，宇文化及以隋將軍陳棱為江都太守，子通率師擊之。

translations.literal: In the beginning Yuwen Huaji appointed the Sui general Chen Ling as prefect of Jiangdu — Zitong led troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji had appointed the Sui general Chen Ling prefect of Jiangdu, and Zitong led his army against him.

sentences.zh: 棱南求救於沈法興，西乞師於杜伏威，二人各以兵至，伏威屯清流，法興保楊子，相去數十里間。

translations.literal: Ling southward sought rescue from Shen Faxing, westward begged troops from Du Fuwei — the two men each came with troops; Fuwei camped at Qingliu, Faxing held Yangzi — separated by several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ling appealed south to Shen Faxing and west to Du Fuwei for reinforcements. Both came with their armies — Fuwei encamped at Qingliu and Faxing held Yangzi, some tens of li apart.

sentences.zh: 子通納言毛文深進計，募江南人詐為法興之兵，夜襲伏威。

translations.literal: Zitong's Remonstrance Director Mao Wenshen advanced a plan: recruit Jiangnan men to feign as Faxing's troops and night-raid Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong's Remonstrance Director Mao Wenshen devised a stratagem to recruit Jiangnan men disguised as Faxing's soldiers for a night attack on Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 伏威不悟，恨法興之侵己，又遣兵襲法興。

translations.literal: Fuwei did not perceive it; he resented Faxing's encroachment on himself and again dispatched troops to raid Faxing.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei did not see through the ruse. Believing Faxing had attacked him, he sent troops against Faxing in turn.

sentences.zh: 二人相疑，莫敢先動。

translations.literal: The two men suspected each other — none dared move first.
translations.idiomatic: Mutual suspicion kept both armies motionless.

sentences.zh: 子通遂得盡銳攻陷江都，陳棱奔於伏威。

translations.literal: Zitong thereupon was able to deploy all his elite strength, attack and capture Jiangdu — Chen Ling fled to Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong then threw his full strength into the assault, captured Jiangdu, and Chen Ling fled to Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 子通入據江都，盡虜其眾，因僭即皇帝位，國稱吳，建元為明政。

translations.literal: Zitong entered and held Jiangdu, fully captured his masses; thereupon usurped the emperor's position — state styled Wu, era name established as Mingzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong seized Jiangdu, absorbed Chen Ling's entire force, and proclaimed himself emperor of Wu with the era name Mingzheng.

sentences.zh: 丹陽賊帥樂伯通率眾萬餘來降，子通拜尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: The Danyang bandit chief Yue Botong leading more than ten thousand came to surrender — Zitong appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Danyang bandit chief Yue Botong surrendered with more than ten thousand followers, and Zitong appointed him Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 更進擊法興於庱亭，斬其僕射蔣元超，法興棄城宵遁，遂有晉陵之地。

translations.literal: Again he advanced to attack Faxing at Tingting, beheaded his Vice Director Jiang Yuanchao; Faxing abandoned the city and fled by night — he thereupon held Jiling commandery's lands.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced again against Faxing at Tingting, killed Faxing's Vice Director Jiang Yuanchao, and drove Faxing from the city in a night flight, securing Jiling.

sentences.zh: 獲法興府掾李百藥，引為內史侍郎，使典文翰；

translations.literal: He captured Faxing's bureau aide Li Baiyao, drew him in as Secretariat Vice Director, and had him oversee documents;
translations.idiomatic: He captured Faxing's aide Li Baiyao and appointed him Secretariat Vice Director in charge of documents;

sentences.zh: 以法興尚書左丞殷芊為太常卿，使掌禮樂。

translations.literal: he took Faxing's Left Assistant Director Yin Qian as Minister of Ceremonies and had him manage rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: he made Faxing's former Left Assistant Director Yin Qian Minister of Ceremonies to oversee rites and music.

sentences.zh: 由是隋郡縣及江南人士多歸之。

translations.literal: From this the Sui commanderies and counties and Jiangnan scholars largely came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter many officials and gentry from the former Sui commanderies and Jiangnan submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 後伏威遣輔公祏攻陷丹陽，進屯溧水，子通擊之，反為公祏所敗。

translations.literal: Later Fuwei sent Fu Gongshi to attack and capture Danyang, advanced to camp at Lishui — Zitong attacked him but in turn was defeated by Gongshi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fuwei sent Fu Gongshi to take Danyang and advance to Lishui. Zitong attacked him but was defeated.

sentences.zh: 又屬糧盡，子通棄江都，保於京口，江西之地盡歸伏威。

translations.literal: Again his food ran out; Zitong abandoned Jiangdu, held at Jingkou — the lands west of the river all returned to Fuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies ran out, and Zitong abandoned Jiangdu for Jingkou while all the territory west of the river fell to Fuwei.

sentences.zh: 子通又東走太湖，鳩集亡散，得二萬人，襲沈法興於吳郡，破之，率其官屬都於餘杭。

translations.literal: Zitong again fled east to Taihu, mustered scattered fugitives, gained twenty thousand men, raided Shen Faxing at Wujun, defeated him, and led his civil and military officials to establish their capital at Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zitong fled east to Lake Tai, rallied scattered survivors to twenty thousand men, routed Shen Faxing at Wujun, and moved his court to Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 東至會稽，南至千嶺，西距宣城，北至太湖，盡有其地。

translations.literal: East to Kuaiji, south to Qianling, west to Xuancheng, north to Taihu — he fully possessed these lands.
translations.idiomatic: His domain stretched east to Kuaiji, south to Qianling, west to Xuancheng, and north to Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 未幾，杜伏威遣其將王雄誕攻之，大戰於蘇州，子通敗績，退保餘杭。

translations.literal: Before long Du Fuwei sent his general Wang Xiongdan to attack him — great battle at Suzhou; Zitong suffered defeat, withdrew to hold Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Du Fuwei's general Wang Xiongdan attacked him. After a great battle at Suzhou, Zitong was defeated and retreated to Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 雄誕進逼之，戰於城下，軍覆敗，子通窮蹙請降。

translations.literal: Xiongdan pressed him — battle below the walls; the army was utterly defeated; Zitong in dire straits requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongdan pressed the siege and defeated him beneath the walls. Cornered, Zitong offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 伏威執之，並其左僕射樂伯通送於京師，盡收其地。

translations.literal: Fuwei seized him, together with his Left Vice Director Yue Botong sent to the capital — fully recovered his lands.
translations.idiomatic: Fuwei took him captive, along with his Left Vice Director Yue Botong, and sent them to the capital, recovering all of Zitong's territory.

sentences.zh: 高祖不之罪，賜宅一區、公田五頃，禮賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu did not punish him, bestowed one residence district and five qing of public fields — ritual gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu did not punish him but granted him a residence and five qing of public land with generous honors.

sentences.zh: 及伏威來朝，子通謂伯通曰：「伏威既來，東方未靜，我所部兵，多在江外，往彼收之，可有大功於天下矣。

translations.literal: When Fuwei came to court, Zitong said to Botong: "Fuwei having come, the east is not yet calm — the troops under my command largely are beyond the river; going there to gather them, one could achieve great merit for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuwei came to court, Zitong said to Botong, "With Fuwei at the capital the east is still unsettled. Most of my troops remain beyond the Yangzi. If we go and rally them, we could win great merit under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」遂相與亡，至藍田關，為吏所獲，與伯通俱伏誅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon together they fled; reaching Lantian Pass they were seized by officials — together with Botong both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: " They fled together but were captured at Lantian Pass and executed along with Botong.

sentences.zh: 時又有朱粲、林士弘、張善安，皆僭號於江、淮之間。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Zhu Can, Lin Shihong, and Zhang Shian — all usurped titles between the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Around the same time Zhu Can, Lin Shihong, and Zhang Shian all proclaimed themselves rulers in the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 朱粲朱粲者，亳州城父人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Can — Zhu Can was a native of Chengfu in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Can was a native of Chengfu in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 初為縣佐史。

translations.literal: At first he was a county clerical assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun as a county clerical assistant.

sentences.zh: 大業末，從軍討長白山賊，遂聚結為群盜，號「可達寒賊」，自稱迦樓羅王，眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he followed the army to attack the Changbai Mountain bandits — thereupon gathered and formed a gang of robbers, styled "Kedahan Bandits," called himself King Garuda — masses reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he joined the campaign against the Changbai Mountain bandits, then gathered a band of robbers calling themselves the Kedahan Bandits. He styled himself King Garuda and gathered more than a hundred thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 引軍渡淮，屠竟陵、沔陽，後轉掠山南，郡縣不能守，所至殺戮，噍類無遺。

translations.literal: He led troops across the Huai, massacred Jingling and Mianyang — later turned to plunder Shannan; commanderies and counties could not hold — wherever he went slaughter, not even a jawbone left behind.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Huai and massacred the populations of Jingling and Mianyang, then ravaged the lands south of the mountains. Counties could not hold him, and his armies slaughtered everyone in their path without exception.

sentences.zh: 義寧中，招慰使馬元規擊破之。

translations.literal: In Yining, the pacification commissioner Ma Yuangui attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yining era the pacification commissioner Ma Yuangui defeated him.

sentences.zh: 俄而收輯餘眾，兵又大盛，僭稱楚帝於冠軍，建元為昌達，攻陷鄧州，有眾二十萬。

translations.literal: Soon he gathered remaining masses — troops again great prosperity; usurped title Emperor of Chu at Guanjun, era name Changda, attacked and captured Dengzhou — had masses two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He soon reassembled his force, proclaimed himself Emperor of Chu at Guanjun with the era name Changda, captured Dengzhou, and commanded two hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 粲所克州縣，皆發其藏粟以充食，遷徙無常，去輒焚余貲，毀城郭，又不務稼穡，以劫掠為業。

translations.literal: In whatever commanderies and counties Can captured he all issued stored grain for food; migrations had no constancy — on leaving he burned surplus goods, destroyed walls and cities; again he did not attend to planting — plunder was his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: In every county he seized he emptied the granaries for provisions, moved constantly, burned what he could not carry, and destroyed city walls. He scorned agriculture and lived by plunder alone.

sentences.zh: 於是百姓大餒，死者如積，人多相食。

translations.literal: Thereupon the common people great famine — dead piled like heaps; many men ate one another.
translations.idiomatic: The people starved. Corpses piled in heaps, and cannibalism became widespread.

sentences.zh: 軍中罄竭，無所虜掠，乃取嬰兒蒸而啖之，因令軍士曰：「食之美者，寧過於人肉乎！

translations.literal: In the army all was exhausted, nothing to plunder — he then took infants, steamed them and ate them; thereupon told the soldiers: "Of foods that are fine, could any surpass human flesh!
translations.idiomatic: When his army's supplies were exhausted and there was nothing left to plunder, he had infants steamed and eaten, then told his soldiers, "Among delicacies, what could surpass human flesh!

sentences.zh: 但令他國有人，我何所慮？

translations.literal: Only let other states have people — what have we to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: As long as other lands still have people, what do we have to fear?

sentences.zh: 」即勒所部，有略得婦人小兒皆烹之，分給軍士，乃稅諸城堡，取小弱男女以益兵糧。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered his subordinates: any women and children seized in raids were all boiled and distributed to the soldiers; then he levied on all walled forts, taking weak young men and women to supplement army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered that any women or children taken in raids be cooked and distributed to the troops, and levied the walled towns for boys and girls to supplement his army's rations.

sentences.zh: 隋著作佐郎陸從典、通事舍人顏愍楚因譴左遷，並在南陽，粲悉引之為賓客，後遭飢餒，合家為賊所啖。

translations.literal: The Sui Assistant Editorial Director Lu Congdian and Communications Attendant Yan Mintu, because of censure demoted to the left, were both at Nanyang — Can fully drew them in as guests; later they encountered famine — whole families were eaten by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui officials Lu Congdian, Assistant Editorial Director, and Yan Mintu, Communications Attendant, had been demoted to Nanyang for disciplinary offenses. Can took them both as retainers, but in the famine that followed his men devoured their entire households.

sentences.zh: 又諸城懼稅，皆相攜逃散。

translations.literal: Again all the walled towns feared the levy — all mutually led one another and fled scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Towns throughout his domain fled en masse for fear of his levies.

sentences.zh: 顯州首領楊士林、田瓚率兵以背粲，諸州響應，相聚而攻之，大戰於淮源。

translations.literal: The Xianzhou chieftains Yang Shilin and Tian Zan led troops to turn their backs on Can — the various prefectures responded in echo, gathered to attack him — great battle at Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianzhou leaders Yang Shilin and Tian Zan rebelled against him, and other prefectures rose in response. They joined forces and met him in a great battle at Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 粲敗，以數千兵奔於菊潭縣，遣使請降。

translations.literal: Can was defeated, with several thousand troops fled to Jutan county, dispatched envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Can was defeated and fled to Jutan county with a few thousand men, then sent envoys to offer surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖令假散騎常侍段確迎勞之，確因醉，侮粲曰：「聞卿啖人，作何滋味？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered the Acting Regular Attendant Duan Que to welcome and comfort him — Que, because drunk, insulted Can saying: "I hear you eat people — what is the flavor?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent the Acting Regular Attendant Duan Que to receive him. Que, drunk, mocked Can, saying, "I hear you eat human flesh — how does it taste?

sentences.zh: 」粲曰：「若啖嗜酒之人，正似糟藏豬肉。

translations.literal: " Can said: "If one eats those who love wine, it is just like pork pickled in lees.
translations.idiomatic: " Can replied, "If you eat a drunkard, it is like pork cured in wine lees.

sentences.zh: 」確怒，慢罵曰：「狂賊，入朝後一頭奴耳，更得啖人乎！

translations.literal: " Que grew angry, contemptuously cursed saying: "Mad bandit — after entering court nothing but a slave's head — can you still eat people!
translations.idiomatic: " Que flew into a rage and sneered, "Mad bandit! Once you reach court you'll be nothing but a slave — will you still eat people then!

sentences.zh: 」粲懼，於坐收確及從者數十人，奔於王世充，拜為龍驤大將軍。

translations.literal: " Can feared; at the seat he seized Que and several tens of followers, fled to Wang Shichong, was appointed Dragon-Charger Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: " Terrified, Can seized Que and several dozen attendants at the banquet and fled to Wang Shichong, who appointed him Dragon-Charger Grand General.

sentences.zh: 東都平，獲之，斬於洛水之上。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified he was captured and beheaded above the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was pacified he was captured and beheaded on the banks of the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 士庶嫉其殘忍，競投瓦礫以擊其屍，須臾封之若冢。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners hated his cruelty — competing to cast tiles and stones to strike his corpse; in a moment it was sealed like a tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners, loathing his cruelty, pelted his corpse with tiles and stones until it was heaped like a tomb.

sentences.zh: 林士弘林士弘者，饒州鄱陽人也。

translations.literal: Lin Shihong — Lin Shihong was a native of Poyang in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Shihong was a native of Poyang in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 大業十二年，與其鄉人操師乞起為群盜。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye he with his fellow-villager Cao Shiji rose as a gang of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Daye era he and his fellow villager Cao Shiji raised a band of robbers.

sentences.zh: 師乞自號元興王，攻陷豫章郡而據之，以士弘為大將軍。

translations.literal: Shiji styled himself King of Yuanxing, attacked and captured Yuzhang commandery and held it, making Shihong Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji styled himself King of Yuanxing, seized Yuzhang commandery, and appointed Shihong Grand General.

sentences.zh: 隋遣持書侍御史劉子翊率師討之，師乞中矢而死。

translations.literal: Sui dispatched the Attendant Censor Bearing Documents Liu Ziyi leading troops to attack him — Shiji was struck by an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui sent the Attendant Censor Bearing Documents Liu Ziyi against him. Shiji was struck by an arrow and killed.

sentences.zh: 士弘代董其眾，復與子翊大戰於彭蠡湖，隋師敗績，子翊死之。

translations.literal: Shihong replaced him in directing the masses, again with Ziyi great battle at Poyang Lake — Sui troops suffered defeat, Ziyi died.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong took command of his force and fought Liu Ziyi again on Poyang Lake. The Sui army was routed and Ziyi was killed.

sentences.zh: 士弘大振，兵至十餘萬。

translations.literal: Shihong greatly prospered — troops reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong's power swelled until his army numbered more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 大業十三年，徙據虔州，自稱皇帝，國號楚，建元太平，以其黨王戎為司空。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daye he moved to hold Qianzhou, styled himself emperor — state name Chu, era name Taiping — made his partisan Wang Rong Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Daye he moved his base to Qianzhou, proclaimed himself emperor of Chu with the era name Taiping, and appointed his follower Wang Rong Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 攻陷臨川、廬陵、南康、宜春等諸郡，北至九江，南洎番禺，悉有其地。

translations.literal: He attacked and captured Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, Yichun and other commanderies — north to Jiujiang, south reaching Panyu — fully possessed these lands.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Linchuan, Luling, Nankang, Yichun, and other commanderies, holding all the territory from Jiujiang in the north to Panyu in the south.

sentences.zh: 其黨張善安保南康郡，懷貳於士弘，以舟師循江而下，擊破豫章。

translations.literal: His partisan Zhang Shian guarded Nankang commandery, harbored double loyalty toward Shihong — with a river fleet followed the river downstream and broke Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Zhang Shian held Nankang commandery but harbored divided loyalties. He led a fleet downriver and seized Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 士弘尚有南昌、虔、循、潮數州之地。

translations.literal: Shihong still had the lands of several prefectures: Nanchang, Qian, Xun, and Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong still held Nanchang, Qian, Xun, and Chao prefectures.

sentences.zh: 及蕭銑破後，散兵稍往歸之，士弘復振。

translations.literal: When Xiao Xian was broken afterward, scattered troops gradually went to join him — Shihong again prospered.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiao Xian's defeat, scattered troops gradually rallied to him and Shihong revived his power.

sentences.zh: 荊州總管趙王孝恭遣使招慰之，其循、潮二州並來降。

translations.literal: The Jingzhou area commander Prince Zhao Xiaogong dispatched envoys to summon and comfort him — his Xun and Chao two prefectures both came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Xiaogong, area commander of Jingzhou, sent envoys to win him over, and his Xun and Chao prefectures submitted.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，士弘遣其弟鄱陽王藥師率兵二萬攻圍循州，刺史楊略與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wude, Shihong sent his younger brother the Prince of Poyang Yaoshi leading twenty thousand troops to besiege Xunzhou — prefect Yang Lue fought him — great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wude, Shihong sent his brother the Prince of Poyang, Yaoshi, with twenty thousand men to besiege Xunzhou. Prefect Yang Lue defeated him utterly.

sentences.zh: 士弘懼而遁走，潛保於安城之山洞。

translations.literal: Shihong feared and fled — secretly held at a mountain cave in Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong fled in fear and hid in a mountain cave near Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 王戎亦以南昌來降，拜為南昌州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Rong also with Nanchang came to surrender — was appointed prefect of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong also surrendered Nanchang and was appointed prefect of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 戎於是召士弘藏之於宅，招誘舊兵，更謀作亂。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon summoned Shihong and hid him in his residence, recruited and enticed old troops, again plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Rong then summoned Shihong and hid him in his house, rallied former soldiers, and plotted another uprising.

sentences.zh: 其年，洪州總管張善安密知其事，發兵討之，會士弘死，部兵潰散，戎為善安所虜。

translations.literal: That year the Hongzhou area commander Zhang Shian secretly learned of the affair, sent troops to attack — it happened that Shihong died, his division troops scattered in defeat, Rong was captured by Shian.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Hongzhou area commander Zhang Shian learned of the plot and attacked. Shihong died in the fighting, his troops scattered, and Rong was captured by Shian.

sentences.zh: 張善安張善安者，兗州方與人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shian — Zhang Shian was a native of Fangyu in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shian was a native of Fangyu in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十七便為劫盜，轉掠淮南，有眾百餘人。

translations.literal: At age seventeen he was already a robber-bandit, turned to plunder Huainan — had masses of more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he had already turned to banditry and raided Huainan with a band of more than a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 會孟讓為王世充所破，其散卒稍歸之，得八百人。

translations.literal: It happened that Meng Rang was defeated by Wang Shichong — his scattered soldiers gradually came over to him; he gained eight hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Rang was defeated by Wang Shichong, his scattered troops gradually joined Shian until he had eight hundred men.

sentences.zh: 襲破廬江郡，因渡江，附林士弘於豫章。

translations.literal: He raided and broke Lujiang commandery, then crossed the river, attached to Lin Shihong at Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He raided and captured Lujiang commandery, crossed the Yangzi, and joined Lin Shihong at Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 士弘不信之，營於南塘上。

translations.literal: Shihong did not trust him — camped on the south embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Shihong distrusted him and encamped on the south bank of the pond.

sentences.zh: 善安憾之，襲擊士弘，焚其郛郭。

translations.literal: Shian resented this, raided and attacked Shihong, burned his outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Shian, resenting this treatment, attacked Shihong and burned his outer defenses.

sentences.zh: 而士弘後去豫章，善安復來據之，仍以其地歸國，授洪州總管。

translations.literal: But Shihong later left Yuzhang — Shian again came to hold it, still with his lands submitted to the state — was appointed Hongzhou area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Shihong later withdrew from Yuzhang, Shian seized it again and submitted the territory to the Tang, receiving appointment as Hongzhou area commander.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏之反也，善安亦舉兵相應，公祏以為西南道大行台。

translations.literal: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, Shian also raised troops in response — Gongshi made him Southwest Circuit Grand Marshal's Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gongshi rebelled, Shian also rose in support and was made Grand Marshal of the Southwest Circuit on Gongshi's staff.

sentences.zh: 安撫使李大亮以兵擊之，兩軍隔水而陣，大亮諭以禍福。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner Li Daliang with troops attacked him — the two armies faced each other across the water in formation; Daliang instructed him on fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commissioner Li Daliang attacked him. The two armies faced each other across the water while Daliang urged him to consider the consequences.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「善安無背逆之心，但為將士所誤。

translations.literal: He replied: "Shian has no heart of rebellion — only was misled by officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Shian has no heart for rebellion but was led astray by his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 今欲歸降，又恐不免於死。

translations.literal: Now wishing to return and surrender, again I fear I cannot escape death.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to surrender, yet I fear I will not escape execution.

sentences.zh: 」大亮謂曰：「張總管既有降心，吾亦不相疑阻。

translations.literal: " Daliang said to him: "Area Commander Zhang already has a heart to surrender — I also will not suspect or obstruct.
translations.idiomatic: " Daliang said, "Since Area Commander Zhang already wishes to surrender, I will not stand in your way.

sentences.zh: 」因獨身逾澗就之，入其陣，與善安握手交言，示無猜意。

translations.literal: " Thereupon alone he crossed the stream to go to him, entered his formation, clasped hands with Shian and conversed — showing no suspicious intent.
translations.idiomatic: " He then crossed the stream alone, entered Shian's camp, shook his hand, and spoke with him openly to show he meant no treachery.

sentences.zh: 善安大喜，因許降，將數十騎至大亮營，大亮引之而入，因令武士執之，從者遁走。

translations.literal: Shian greatly rejoiced, thereupon promised surrender, leading several tens of horsemen to Daliang's camp — Daliang led him in, then ordered warriors to seize him; followers fled scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Shian was overjoyed and agreed to surrender. He came to Daliang's camp with several dozen horsemen. Daliang ushered him in, then had his warriors seize him while his escort fled.

sentences.zh: 既而送善安於長安，稱不與公祏交通，高祖初善遇之。

translations.literal: Soon after he sent Shian to Chang'an; he claimed no communication with Gongshi — Emperor Gaozu at first treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Chang'an, where he claimed he had had no dealings with Gongshi. Emperor Gaozu at first treated him kindly.

sentences.zh: 及公祏敗，搜得其書，與相往復，遂誅之。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was defeated they searched and obtained his letters — mutual correspondence back and forth — he was thereupon executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongshi was defeated, a search uncovered letters exchanged between them, and Shian was executed.

sentences.zh: 羅藝羅藝，字子延，本襄陽人也，寓居京兆之雲陽。

translations.literal: Luo Yi — Luo Yi, style Ziyan, originally a native of Xiangyang, sojourned dwelling in Yunyang of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi, style name Ziyan, was originally from Xiangyang but had settled in Yunyang in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父榮，隋監門將軍。

translations.literal: His father Rong was a Sui Gate Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong had been a Gate Guard General under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 藝性桀黠，剛愎不仁，勇於攻戰，善射，能弄槊。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was fierce and cunning, obstinate and unkind, brave in attack and battle, skilled at archery, able to wield the lance.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was fierce and cunning, obstinate and cruel, bold in battle, an expert archer, and skilled with the lance.

sentences.zh: 大業時，屢以軍功官至虎賁郎將，煬帝令受右武衛大將軍李景節度，督軍於北平。

translations.literal: In the Daye era, repeatedly through military merit he reached the post of Tiger-Fierce Commandant; Emperor Yang ordered him to accept the Right Martial Guard Grand General Li Jing's command and control, supervising troops at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he rose through repeated military achievements to Tiger-Fierce Commandant. Emperor Yang placed him under the command of Li Jing, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, to supervise troops at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 藝少習戎旅，分部嚴肅，然任氣縱暴，每凌侮於景，頻為景所辱，藝深銜之。

translations.literal: Yi from youth practiced military campaigns — his divisions were stern and solemn; yet he indulged his temper and was violent, every time insulting and humiliating Jing — frequently was humiliated by Jing — Yi deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Trained from youth in military affairs, Yi ran a tight and disciplined command, but he was headstrong and violent and constantly insulted Li Jing. Jing in turn frequently humiliated him, and Yi nursed a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 後遇天下大亂，涿郡物殷阜，加有伐遼器仗，倉粟盈積。

translations.literal: Later he encountered the realm's great disorder — Zhuo commandery's goods were abundant and rich; moreover there were weapons for the Liaodong campaign — granary grain overflowed in accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire fell into chaos, Zhuo commandery was rich in goods and stocked with weapons for the Liaodong campaign and overflowing granaries.

sentences.zh: 又臨朔宮中多珍產，屯兵數萬，而諸賊競來侵掠。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the Lingshuo Palace there were many rare products; tens of thousands of troops were stationed, yet the various bandits vied to come raiding and plundering.
translations.idiomatic: The Lingshuo Palace nearby held a wealth of rare goods, and tens of thousands of soldiers were encamped there, yet bandits from every direction pressed in to raid.

sentences.zh: 留守官虎賁郎將趙什住、賀蘭誼、晉文衍等皆不能拒，唯藝獨出戰，前後破賊不可勝計，威勢日重。

translations.literal: The garrison officials — Tiger Elite Gentlemen Zhao Shizhu, Helan Yi, Jin Wenyian, and the rest — all could not repel them; only Yi alone went out to fight; before and after he broke the bandits in numbers beyond counting; his awesome power grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison officers Zhao Shizhu, Helan Yi, and Jin Wenyian, all Tiger Elite guards, could not hold them off. Luo Yi alone took the field, defeating bandits in countless engagements until his prestige grew daily.

sentences.zh: 什住等頗忌藝，藝陰知之，將圖為亂，乃宣言於眾曰：「吾輩討賊，甚有功效，城中倉庫山積，制在留守之官，而無心濟貧，此豈存恤之意也！

translations.literal: Shizhu and the others greatly envied Yi; Yi knew it in secret and planned to stir rebellion; he thereupon proclaimed to the multitude, saying: "We in fighting the bandits have achieved great merit; in the city the storehouses and granaries pile like mountains; control rests with the garrison officials — yet they have no mind to aid the poor — is this the intent of cherishing and showing mercy!
translations.idiomatic: Shizhu and the others grew jealous of Yi. Yi learned of their hostility in secret and planned a revolt. He addressed the troops: "We have fought the bandits with great success, yet the city's granaries overflow while the garrison officers who control them show no concern for the poor. Where is their compassion?

sentences.zh: 」以此言激怒其眾，眾人皆怨。

translations.literal: " With these words he enraged his troops; the multitude all harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: " These words inflamed the soldiers, and resentment spread through the ranks.

sentences.zh: 既而旋師，郡丞出城候藝，藝因執之陳兵，而什住等懼，皆來聽命。

translations.literal: Presently he returned his army; the assistant magistrate came out of the city to await Yi; Yi thereupon seized him and arrayed his troops; Shizhu and the others in fear all came to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: When he marched back, the assistant magistrate came out to receive him. Yi seized him and paraded his troops. Shizhu and the others, in fear, all submitted to his orders.

sentences.zh: 於是發庫物以賜戰士，開倉以賑窮乏，境內咸悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he distributed treasury goods to reward the warriors, opened the granaries to relieve the destitute — throughout the territory all were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed weapons from the arsenal to his soldiers, opened the granaries to feed the needy, and won the loyalty of the entire region.

sentences.zh: 殺渤海太守唐禕等不同己者數人，威振邊朔，柳城、懷遠並歸附之。

translations.literal: He killed several who differed from him, such as Bohai grand administrator Tang Yi and others; his authority shook the northern frontier; Liucheng and Huaiyuan both submitted and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: He executed several dissenters, including the Bohai prefect Tang Yi. His authority dominated the northern frontier, and Liucheng and Huaiyuan both submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 藝黜柳城太守楊林甫，改郡為營州，以襄平太守鄧暠為總管，藝自稱幽州總管。

translations.literal: Yi removed Liucheng grand administrator Yang Linpu, changed the commandery to Yingzhou, appointed Xiangping grand administrator Deng Hao as chief commander — Yi styled himself Chief Commander of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi deposed the Liucheng prefect Yang Linpu, reorganized the commandery as Yingzhou, appointed Deng Hao of Xiangping as regional commander, and styled himself Chief Commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及至山東，遣使召藝，藝曰：「我隋室舊臣，感恩累葉，大行顛覆，實所痛心。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji reached Shandong and sent envoys to summon Yi; Yi said: "I am an old servant of the Sui house — grace received through successive generations; the Great Lineage's overthrow is truly what pains my heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji reached Shandong, he sent envoys to summon Luo Yi. Yi replied: "I am a longtime servant of the Sui dynasty, indebted through generations to the throne. The ruin of the imperial house grieves me deeply.

sentences.zh: 」乃斬化及使者，而為煬帝發喪，大臨三日。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he beheaded Huaji's envoy, and for Emperor Yang held mourning rites, with a great lamentation for three days.
translations.idiomatic: " He then executed Yuwen Huaji's envoy, held funeral rites for Emperor Yang, and mourned for three days.

sentences.zh: 竇建德、高開道亦遣使於藝，藝謂官屬曰：「建德、開道，皆劇賊耳，化及弒逆，並不可從。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao also sent envoys to Yi; Yi said to his officials: "Jiande and Kaidao are both fierce bandits; Huaji regicide and treason — none may be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande and Gao Kaidao also sent envoys. Yi told his staff: "Jiande and Kaidao are nothing but violent rebels, and Yuwen Huaji is a regicide — we must follow none of them.

sentences.zh: 今唐公起兵，皆符人望，入據關右，事無不成。

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Tang has raised troops — all accord with men's hopes; he has entered and held Guanxi — the affair cannot fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tang has raised his banners in accord with the people's wishes, holds the Guanzhong region, and cannot fail to prevail.

sentences.zh: 吾率眾歸之，意已決矣，有沮眾異議者必戮之。

translations.literal: I shall lead the multitude to submit to him — my mind is already decided; whoever discourages the masses with dissenting words shall surely be executed.
translations.idiomatic: I have decided to lead our forces to submit to him. Anyone who dissents and discourages the troops shall be put to death.

sentences.zh: 」會我使人張道源綏輯山東，遣人諭意，藝大悅。

translations.literal: " It happened that our envoy Zhang Daoyuan was pacifying Shandong and sent someone to convey the intent — Yi was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " It happened that the Tang envoy Zhang Daoyuan was organizing Shandong and sent a messenger with the court's invitation. Yi was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，奉表歸國，詔封燕王，賜姓李氏，預宗正屬籍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude he presented a memorial submitting to the state; an edict enfeoffed him as Prince of Yan, bestowed the surname Li, and entered him in the genealogy rolls of the Directorate of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wude he submitted a memorial pledging allegiance. The Emperor enfeoffed him as Prince of Yan, granted him the surname Li, and entered his name in the imperial clan registers.

sentences.zh: 太宗之擊劉黑闥也，藝領本兵數萬，破黑闥弟什善於徐河，俘斬八千人。

translations.literal: When the Taizong attacked Liu Heita, Yi led his native troops numbering tens of thousands, broke Heita's younger brother Shishan at the Xu River, captured and beheaded eight thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned against Liu Heita, Yi led tens of thousands of his own troops, defeated Heita's brother Shishan at the Xu River, and killed or captured eight thousand men.

sentences.zh: 明年，黑闥引突厥俱入寇，藝復將兵與隱太子建成會於洺州，因請入朝，高祖遇之甚厚，俄拜左翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The next year Heita led the Turks together in invasion; Yi again led troops and met with the Hidden Crown Prince Jiancheng at Mingzhou; he thereupon requested to enter court audience; Gaozu received him very generously; shortly he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Yuyi Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Heita led Turkic allies in another invasion. Yi again took the field and joined Crown Prince Jiancheng at Mingzhou. He then requested an audience at court. Gaozu received him warmly and soon appointed him General-in-Chief of the Left Yuyi Guard.

sentences.zh: 藝自以功高位重，無所降下，太宗左右嘗至其營，藝無故毆擊之。

translations.literal: Yi considered himself of meritorious service and high position with none to whom he would lower himself; Taizong's attendants once came to his camp — Yi for no reason beat them.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his merit and high rank, Yi deferred to no one. When some of Taizong's attendants visited his camp, he beat them without provocation.

sentences.zh: 高祖怒，以屬吏，久而乃釋，待之如初。

translations.literal: Gaozu was angry and handed him over to the law officers; after a long while he was then released, treated as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was furious and turned him over to the judicial officers. After a long detention he was released and treated as before.

sentences.zh: 時突厥屢為寇患，以藝素有威名，為北夷所憚，令以本官領天節軍將鎮涇州。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly made raiding troubles; because Yi from old had a renowned awesome name and was feared by the northern barbarians, he was ordered to hold his former office and lead the Tianjie Army as general guarding Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks raided repeatedly in those years. Because Yi's longstanding reputation terrified the northern tribes, he was ordered to keep his rank, command the Tianjie Army, and guard Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，拜開府儀同三司，而藝懼不自安，遂於涇州詐言閱武，因追兵，矯稱奉密詔勒兵入朝，率眾軍至於豳州。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, Yi was appointed Senior Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and the Vicissitude Tricorn; yet Yi feared and was not at ease; he thereupon at Jingzhou falsely claimed review of arms, thereupon mustered pursuing troops, falsely styled that he received a secret edict ordering troops to enter court audience — leading massed armies to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Yi was made Senior Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal. Uneasy and afraid, he staged a military review at Jingzhou, rallied his troops under a forged secret edict ordering them to march on the capital, and advanced to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 治中趙慈皓不知藝反，馳出謁之，藝遂入據豳州。

translations.literal: Assistant Administrator Zhao Cihao did not know Yi had rebelled; he galloped out to pay respects to him — Yi thereupon entered and seized Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant administrator Zhao Cihao, unaware of the rebellion, rode out to greet him. Yi seized Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗命吏部尚書長孫無忌、右武候大將軍尉遲敬德率眾討藝。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Minister of Personnel Zhangsun Wuji and General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard Yuchi Jingde to lead the masses in punishing Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered the Minister of Personnel Zhangsun Wuji and General Yuchi Jingde to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 王師未至，慈皓與統軍楊岌潛謀擊之，事洩，藝執慈皓繫獄。

translations.literal: The royal army had not yet arrived; Cihao together with Commanding General Yang Ji secretly plotted to strike him — the affair leaked out; Yi seized Cihao and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Before the imperial army arrived, Cihao and the commanding general Yang Ji plotted a surprise attack, but the plan was discovered. Yi seized Cihao and threw him in prison.

sentences.zh: 岌時在城外，覺變，遽勒兵攻之，藝大潰，棄妻子，與數百騎奔於突厥。

translations.literal: Ji at that time was outside the city; sensing the change, he urgently mustered troops to attack him — Yi was greatly routed; he abandoned wife and children; with several hundred horsemen he fled to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ji, outside the walls, sensed the plot and attacked at once. Yi was routed utterly, abandoned his family, and fled north with a few hundred horsemen to seek Turkic refuge.

sentences.zh: 至寧州界，過烏氏驛，從者漸散，其左右斬藝，傳首京師，梟之於市。

translations.literal: When he reached the border of Ningzhou, passing Wushi Post, his followers gradually scattered; his attendants beheaded Yi, sent the head to the capital, and exposed it in the market.
translations.idiomatic: At the Ningzhou border, near Wushi Post, his followers deserted him one by one. His own men struck off his head, sent it to the capital, and had it displayed in the market.

sentences.zh: 復其本姓羅氏。

translations.literal: His original surname Luo was restored.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname Luo was restored.

sentences.zh: 藝弟壽，時為利州都督，緣坐伏誅。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Shou, at that time Regional Commander of Lizhou, by connection of guilt was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's brother Shou, then military governor of Lizhou, was executed by association with the crime.

sentences.zh: 先是，曹州女子李氏為五戒，自言通於鬼物，有病癩者，就療多愈，流聞四方，病人自遠而至，門多車騎。

translations.literal: Earlier, a Cao prefecture woman surnamed Li observed the Five Precepts; she claimed herself in communication with ghostly things — those ill with leprosy who came for treatment mostly recovered; report flowed to the four quarters; the sick from afar arrived of themselves; at the gate were many chariots and riders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a Caozhou woman surnamed Li had taken the Five Precepts and claimed communion with spirits. Lepers who sought her treatment were often cured. Fame spread in every direction, and the sick journeyed from far away until chariots and horses crowded her gate.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，詔赴京師。

translations.literal: Gaozu heard of it and issued an edict summoning her to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu heard of her and summoned her to the capital.

sentences.zh: 因往來藝家，謂藝妻孟氏曰：「妃骨相貴不可言，必當母儀天下。

translations.literal: She thereupon came and went to Yi's household, saying to Yi's wife Lady Meng: "Consort, your bone structure is nobly beyond words — you must become the mother model of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: She frequented Yi's household and told his wife Lady Meng: "Your bone structure is too noble for words. You are fated to become empress of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」孟篤信之，命密觀藝，又曰：「妃之貴者，由於王；

translations.literal: " Lady Meng deeply believed her and ordered secret observation of Yi; she again said: "Consort — your nobility comes from the Prince;
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Meng believed her completely and had her husband watched in secret. The woman added: "Your high station depends on the Prince;

sentences.zh: 王貴色發矣，十日間當升大位。

translations.literal: the Prince's noble countenance has already appeared — within ten days he should ascend to the great position.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince's royal bearing has already emerged. Within ten days he will take the throne.

sentences.zh: 」孟氏由是遽勸反，孟及李皆坐斬。

translations.literal: " Lady Meng thereby urgently urged rebellion; Meng and Li both by connection were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " Thus urged, Lady Meng pressed her husband to rebel. She and Li were both executed.

sentences.zh: 梁師都梁師都，夏州朔方人也。

translations.literal: Liang Shidu — Liang Shidu was a man of Shuofang in Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Shidu was a native of Shuofang in Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 代為本郡豪族，仕隋鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: For generations his family was the commandery's powerful clan; he served the Sui as Eagle-Brave Gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had dominated the commandery for generations. Under the Sui he held the rank of Eagle-Brave guard officer.

sentences.zh: 大業末，罷歸。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign he left office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 屬盜賊群起，師都陰結徒黨數千人，殺郡丞唐宗，據郡反。

translations.literal: As bandits rose in swarms, Shidu secretly joined several thousand partisans, killed Assistant Magistrate Tang Zong, seized the commandery and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit armies rose everywhere, Shidu secretly gathered several thousand followers, killed the assistant magistrate Tang Zong, and seized the commandery in revolt.

sentences.zh: 自稱大丞相，北連突厥。

translations.literal: He styled himself Grand Chancellor and allied northward with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself Grand Chancellor and allied with the Turks to the north.

sentences.zh: 隋將張世隆擊之，反為所敗。

translations.literal: Sui general Zhang Shilong attacked him and was in turn defeated by him.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui general Zhang Shilong attacked him but was defeated in turn.

sentences.zh: 師都因遣兵掠定雕陰、弘化、延安等郡，於是僭即皇帝位，稱梁國，建元為永隆。

translations.literal: Shidu thereupon sent troops to seize and pacify Diaoyin, Honghua, Yan'an and other commanderies; he thereupon presumptuously ascended the emperor's position, styled his state Liang, and established the era name Yonglong.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu then sent armies to seize Diaoyin, Honghua, Yan'an, and neighboring commanderies, declared himself emperor of a Liang state, and adopted the era name Yonglong.

sentences.zh: 突厥始畢可汗遺以狼頭纛，號為大度毗伽可汗。

translations.literal: The Turkic Khan Shibi sent him a wolf's-head banner and styled him Khan Dadu Pijia.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkic khan Shibi bestowed on him a wolf-head banner and titled him Khan Dadu Pijia.

sentences.zh: 師都乃引突厥居河南之地，攻破鹽川郡。

translations.literal: Shidu thereupon led the Turks to dwell in the territory south of the river, and stormed Yanchuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu then settled Turkic forces south of the Yellow River and captured Yanchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，高祖遣延州總管段德操督兵討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, Gaozu dispatched Yanzhou Chief Commander Duan Decao to supervise troops in punishing him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude, Gaozu sent the Yanzhou commander Duan Decao to lead troops against him.

sentences.zh: 師都與突厥之眾數千騎來寇延安，營於野豬嶺。

translations.literal: Shidu with several thousand Turkic horsemen came to raid Yan'an and encamped at Wild Boar Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu led several thousand Turkic horsemen against Yan'an and encamped at Wild Boar Ridge.

sentences.zh: 德操以眾寡不敵，按甲以挫其銳。

translations.literal: Decao, finding his force few against many, held his armor to blunt their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, Decao held his troops in check to blunt the enemy's momentum.

sentences.zh: 後伺師都稍怠，遣副總管梁禮率眾擊之，德操以輕騎出其不意。

translations.literal: Later, watching for Shidu's slight slackening, he sent Deputy Chief Commander Liang Li to lead the masses in striking him; Decao with light cavalry came out where they did not expect.
translations.idiomatic: When Shidu grew careless, Decao sent his deputy Liang Li to attack while he himself struck with light cavalry from an unexpected quarter.

sentences.zh: 師都與禮酣戰久之，德操多張旗幟，奄至其後，師都大潰，逐北二百餘里，虜男女二百餘口。

translations.literal: Shidu with Li engaged in fierce battle for a long while; Decao set up many banners and flags, suddenly reaching their rear — Shidu was greatly routed; they pursued north more than two hundred li, capturing more than two hundred men and women.
translations.idiomatic: While Shidu and Liang Li battled fiercely, Decao raised a forest of banners and struck from the rear. Shidu fled in rout. The Tang forces pursued him over two hundred li and captured more than two hundred men and women.

sentences.zh: 經數月，師都又以步騎五千來寇，德操擊之，俘斬略盡。

translations.literal: After several months Shidu again with five thousand infantry and cavalry came to raid; Decao struck them — captured and beheaded nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Shidu returned with five thousand foot and horse soldiers. Decao attacked and killed or captured nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 及劉武周之敗，師都大將張舉、劉旻相次來降，師都大懼，遣其尚書陸季覽說處羅可汗曰：「比者中原喪亂，分為數國，勢均力弱，所以北附突厥。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou was defeated, Shidu's great generals Zhang Ju and Liu Min came to surrender one after another; Shidu was greatly afraid; he sent his Minister of State Lu Jilan to persuade Khan Chuluo, saying: "Recently the Central Plains fell into disorder and split into several states — strength equal, power weak — therefore we attached ourselves north to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Wuzhou's defeat, Shidu's generals Zhang Ju and Liu Min surrendered in succession. In alarm, Shidu sent his minister Lu Jilan to urge Khan Chuluo: "The Central Plains have been torn by chaos into rival states too evenly matched to survive alone. That is why we turned north to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 今武周既滅，唐國益大，師都甘從亡破，亦恐次及可汗。

translations.literal: Now Wuzhou is already destroyed — the Tang state grows ever larger; Shidu would willingly follow ruin and destruction — I also fear it will next reach the Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Wuzhou is destroyed, Tang grows stronger daily. Shidu would rather perish than submit, yet I fear the Khan will be next.

sentences.zh: 願可汗行魏孝文之事，遣兵南侵，師都請為鄉導。

translations.literal: I wish the Khan would do as Emperor Xiaowen of Wei did — send troops south to invade — Shidu requests to serve as local guide.
translations.idiomatic: I beg the Khan to follow Emperor Xiaowen of Wei's example, send armies southward into China, and let Shidu guide them as your native scout.

sentences.zh: 」處羅從之。

translations.literal: " Chuluo followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " Chuluo agreed.

sentences.zh: 謀令莫賀咄設入自原州，泥步設與師都入自延州，處羅入自并州，突利可汗與奚、霫、契丹、靺鞨入自幽州，合於竇建德，經滏口道來會於晉、絳。

translations.literal: The plan was to have Moheduo's division enter from Yuanzhou, Nibu's division with Shidu enter from Yanzhou, Chuluo enter from Bingzhou, Khan Tuli with Xi, Xie, Khitan, and Mohe enter from Youzhou — joining with Dou Jiande, passing by the Fuyao gateway road to meet at Jinyang and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: The plan called for Moheduo's division to enter through Yuanzhou, Nibu's division with Shidu through Yanzhou, Chuluo through Bingzhou, and Khan Tuli with the Xi, Khitan, and Mohe through Youzhou. They would join Dou Jiande along the Fuyao route and assemble at Jinyang and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 兵臨發，遇處羅死，乃止。

translations.literal: Troops were on the verge of setting out when they encountered Chuluo's death — and so it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The armies were about to march when Chuluo died, and the campaign was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 高祖又令德操悉發邊兵進擊師都，拔其東城。

translations.literal: Gaozu again ordered Decao to muster all frontier troops in an advance attack on Shidu — they took his eastern citadel.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu again ordered Decao to mobilize all frontier troops, advance on Shidu, and capture his eastern citadel.

sentences.zh: 師都退據西城，又求救於突厥頡利可汗，頡利以勁兵萬騎救援之。

translations.literal: Shidu withdrew to hold the western citadel, again begged rescue from the Turkic Khan Jieli — Jieli with ten thousand crack horsemen came to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu fell back to the western citadel and appealed to the Turkic khan Jieli, who sent ten thousand elite horsemen to his aid.

sentences.zh: 時稽胡大帥劉仚成率眾降師都，師都信讒殺之，於是群情疑懼，多叛師都來降。

translations.literal: At that time the Ji Hu great chief Liu Qian'cheng led his multitude to submit to Shidu; Shidu believed slander and killed him — thereupon the group's hearts were suspicious and afraid; many rebelled against Shidu and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji-hu chieftain Liu Qian'cheng had surrendered to Shidu with his followers, but Shidu believed slanders against him and had him killed. Morale collapsed, and many of his men deserted to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 師都勢蹙，乃往朝頡利，為陳入寇之計。

translations.literal: Shidu's strength was pressed tight; he thereupon went to court audience with Jieli and set forth plans for invasion.
translations.idiomatic: With his power failing, Shidu went in person to Jieli and urged a fresh invasion of China.

sentences.zh: 自此頻致突厥之寇，邊州略無寧歲。

translations.literal: From this time he repeatedly brought Turkic raiders — frontier prefectures briefly had no peaceful year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Turkic raids came repeatedly, and the frontier knew scarcely a year of peace.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗之寇渭橋，亦師都計也。

translations.literal: Khan Jieli's raid on the Wei Bridge was also Shidu's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli's raid on the Wei Bridge was also Shidu's doing.

sentences.zh: 頡利政亂，太宗知師都勢危援孤，以書諭之，不從。

translations.literal: Jieli's government fell into disorder; Taizong knew Shidu's position was perilous, aid isolated — with a letter he instructed him; he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli's court fell into turmoil, Taizong knew Shidu was isolated and desperate. He sent letters urging surrender, but Shidu refused.

sentences.zh: 遣夏州長史劉旻、司馬劉蘭經略之。

translations.literal: He dispatched Xiazhou Senior Recorder Liu Min and Military Affairs Secretary Liu Lan to take charge of the campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Liu Min, administrator of Xiazhou, and Liu Lan, his military affairs secretary, to conduct the campaign.

sentences.zh: 有得其生口者，輒縱遣令為反間，離其君臣之計。

translations.literal: Whenever they captured living mouths among the enemy, they would release and send them back to serve as counter-intelligence, to sunder ruler and minister in stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Captured enemy soldiers were released and turned back as agents of discord to sow distrust between Shidu and his officers.

sentences.zh: 頻選輕騎踐其禾稼，城中漸虛，歸命者相繼，皆善遇之。

translations.literal: They repeatedly selected light cavalry to trample his grain crops; the city gradually grew empty; those submitting came one after another — all were well treated.
translations.idiomatic: Light cavalry repeatedly ravaged his crops. His city grew empty as defectors came in steady streams, and all were treated generously.

sentences.zh: 由是益相猜阻。

translations.literal: From this they increasingly mutually suspected and blocked each other.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion between Shidu and his men deepened.

sentences.zh: 有李正寶、辛獠兒者，皆其名將，謀執師都，事洩不果，正寶竟來降。

translations.literal: There were Li Zhengbao and Xin Liaor — both his famed generals — who plotted to seize Shidu; the affair leaked and did not succeed; Zhengbao in the end came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Two of his best generals, Li Zhengbao and Xin Liaor, plotted to seize him, but the conspiracy failed. Zhengbao defected to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，太宗遣右衛大將軍柴紹、殿中少監薛萬均討之，又使劉旻、劉蘭率勁卒直據朔方東城以逼之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, Taizong dispatched Right Guard General-in-Chief Chai Shao and Palace Supervisor of the Household Junior Monitor Xue Wanjun to punish him; he also sent Liu Min and Liu Lan leading crack troops directly to seize Shuofang's eastern citadel to press him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan, Taizong sent General Chai Shao and Xue Wanjun against him while Liu Min and Liu Lan led elite troops to seize Shuofang's eastern citadel.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗遣兵來援師都，紹逆擊破之，進屯城下。

translations.literal: Khan Jieli dispatched troops to rescue Shidu; Shao met and struck, breaking them; he advanced and encamped below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli sent troops to relieve the siege. Chai Shao repulsed them and encamped beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 師都兵勢日蹙，其從父弟洛仁斬師都，詣紹降，拜洛仁為右驍衛將軍，封朔方郡公。

translations.literal: Shidu's military strength daily grew pressed; his paternal cousin Luoren beheaded Shidu, went to Shao to surrender — Luoren was appointed General of the Right Upright Cavalry Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: As Shidu's army weakened daily, his cousin Luoren slew him and surrendered to Chai Shao. Luoren was made General of the Right Upright Cavalry Guard and enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 師都自起至滅，凡十二歲。

translations.literal: From Shidu's rise to his destruction — altogether twelve years.
translations.idiomatic: From his rise to his fall, Shidu had lasted twelve years.

sentences.zh: 以其地為夏州。

translations.literal: His territory was made Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His territory was reorganized as Xia Province.

sentences.zh: 時又有劉季真、李子和，屯據北邊，與劉武周、梁師都遞為表裡。

translations.literal: At that time there were also Liu Jizhen and Li Zihe — they garrisoned and held the northern frontier, with Liu Wuzhou and Liang Shidu by turns serving as outer and inner mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Liu Jizhen and Li Zihe held the northern frontier in alliance with Liu Wuzhou and Liang Shidu.

sentences.zh: 劉季真劉季真者，離石胡人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jizhen — Liu Jizhen was a Hu man of Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jizhen was a non-Chinese tribesman of Lishi.

sentences.zh: 父龍兒，隋末擁兵數萬，自號劉王，以季真為太子。

translations.literal: His father Long'er, at the end of Sui, held troops numbering tens of thousands, styled himself King Liu, and made Jizhen crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: His father Long'er had raised tens of thousands of troops at the end of the Sui, styled himself King Liu, and named Jizhen his crown prince.

sentences.zh: 龍兒為虎賁郎將梁德所斬，其眾漸散。

translations.literal: Long'er was beheaded by Tiger Elite Gentleman Liang De; his multitude gradually scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Long'er was slain by the Tiger Elite guard Liang De, and his followers dispersed.

sentences.zh: 及義師起，季真與弟六兒復舉兵為盜，引劉武周之眾攻陷石州。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Jizhen with his younger brother Liu'er again raised troops as bandits, leading Liu Wuzhou's masses to storm and take Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang uprising began, Jizhen and his brother Liu'er again took to brigandage, joined Liu Wuzhou, and captured Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 季真北連突厥，自稱突利可汗，以六兒為拓定王，甚為邊患。

translations.literal: Jizhen allied north with the Turks, styled himself Khan Tuli, made Liu'er Prince Tuoding — greatly a frontier menace.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhen allied with the Turks to the north, styled himself Khan Tuli, made Liu'er Prince Tuoding, and became a serious frontier threat.

sentences.zh: 時西河公張綸、真鄉公李仲文俱以兵臨之，季真懼而來降，授石州總管，賜姓李氏，封彭城郡王。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Xihe Zhang Lun and Duke of Zhenxiang Li Zhongwen both with troops pressed upon him — Jizhen in fear came to surrender; he was appointed Chief Commander of Shizhou, bestowed the surname Li, enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Lun of Xihe and Li Zhongwen of Zhenxiang marched against him with armies, Jizhen surrendered in fear. He was made commander of Shizhou, granted the surname Li, and enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 季真見宋金剛與官軍相持於澮州，久而未決，遂親伏武周，與之合勢。

translations.literal: Jizhen saw Song Jingang and the government army locked in stalemate at Fenzhou for a long while without decision — he thereupon personally attached himself to Wuzhou and joined forces with him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Song Jingang and the imperial armies deadlocked at Fenzhou, Jizhen went over to Wuzhou in person and joined his campaign.

sentences.zh: 及金剛敗，季真亡奔高滿政，尋為所殺。

translations.literal: When Jingang was defeated, Jizhen fled in ruin to Gao Manzheng — shortly he was killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingang was defeated, Jizhen fled to Gao Manzheng and was soon killed by him.

sentences.zh: 李子和李子和者，同州蒲城人也。

translations.literal: Li Zihe — Li Zihe was a man of Pucheng in Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zihe was a native of Pucheng in Tong Province.

sentences.zh: 本姓郭氏。

translations.literal: His original surname was Guo.
translations.idiomatic: His family name was originally Guo.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為左翊衛，犯罪徙榆林，見郡內大飢，遂潛引敢死士，得十八人，攻郡門，執郡丞王才，數以不恤百姓，斬之，開倉以賑窮乏。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was in the Left Yuyi Guard; guilty of crime he was banished to Yulin; seeing the commandery interior in great famine, he secretly drew dare-to-die warriors — obtaining eighteen men — stormed the commandery gate, seized Assistant Magistrate Wang Cai, counted out his failure to cherish the common people, beheaded him, opened the granaries to relieve the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daye he served in the Left Yuyi Guard but was banished to Yulin for a crime. Seeing famine grip the commandery, he secretly gathered eighteen daredevils, stormed the gates, seized the assistant magistrate Wang Cai, denounced him for neglecting the people, executed him, and opened the granaries to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 自稱永樂王，建元為正平，尊其父為太公，以弟子政為尚書令，子端、子升為左、右僕射。

translations.literal: He styled himself King of Yongle, established the era name Zhengping, honored his father as Grand Duke, made his younger brother Zizheng Minister of State, and sons Ziduan and Zisheng Left and Right Vice Premiers.
translations.idiomatic: He declared himself King of Yongle, adopted the era name Zhengping, honored his father as Grand Duke, appointed his brother Zizheng as chief minister, and his sons Ziduan and Zisheng as vice premiers.

sentences.zh: 有眾二千餘騎，南連梁師都，北附突厥始畢可汗，並送子為質以自固。

translations.literal: He had a following of more than two thousand horsemen; south he linked with Liang Shidu, north he attached to the Turkic Khan Shibi — both times sending sons as hostages to secure himself.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded more than two thousand horsemen, allied with Liang Shidu to the south and Khan Shibi to the north, sending his sons as hostages to both.

sentences.zh: 始畢先署劉武周為定楊天子，梁師都為解事天子，又以子和為平楊天子，子和固辭不敢當，始畢乃更署子和為屋利設。

translations.literal: Shibi first appointed Liu Wuzhou as Son of Heaven of Dingyang, Liang Shidu as Son of Heaven who Handles Affairs, and again made Zihe Son of Heaven of Pingyang — Zihe firmly declined and dared not accept; Shibi thereupon changed and appointed Zihe as Wuli She.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi had first named Liu Wuzhou Son of Heaven of Dingyang and Liang Shidu Son of Heaven Who Handles Affairs. He offered Zihe the title Son of Heaven of Pingyang, but Zihe refused. Shibi then gave him the Turkic title Wuli She.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，遣使歸款，授榆林郡守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he sent envoys to submit allegiance; he was appointed Administrator of Yulin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude he sent envoys pledging allegiance and was appointed prefect of Yulin.

sentences.zh: 尋就拜雲州總管，封金河郡公。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was appointed on the spot Chief Commander of Yunzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinhe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of Yunzhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinhe.

sentences.zh: 二年，進封郕國公。

translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Bie.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year his rank was raised to Duke of Bie.

sentences.zh: 時師都強暴，子和慮為所攻，尋勒兵襲師都寧朔城，克之。

translations.literal: At that time Shidu was violent and fierce; Zihe feared being attacked by him — shortly he mustered troops and raided Shidu's Ningshuo citadel — and took it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shidu grew violent and aggressive, Zihe feared attack and seized Shidu's citadel at Ningshuo.

sentences.zh: 子和既絕師都，又伺突厥間釁，遣使以聞，為處羅可汗候騎所獲，處羅大怒，囚其弟子升。

translations.literal: Zihe having already severed from Shidu, again watched for a crack in Turkic relations — sent envoys to report; they were captured by Khan Chuluo's scout horsemen — Chuluo was greatly angry and imprisoned his younger son Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Having broken with Shidu, Zihe watched for a rift with the Turks and sent messengers to report it. Chuluo's scouts captured them. Enraged, Chuluo imprisoned Zihe's son Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 子和自以孤危，甚懼。

translations.literal: Zihe considered himself isolated and perilous — greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling isolated and exposed, Zihe was deeply afraid.

sentences.zh: 四年，拔戶口南徙，詔以延州故城居之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he uprooted households and moved south; an edict made them dwell in Yanzhou's old city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he moved his people south. An edict settled them in Yanzhou's abandoned city.

sentences.zh: 五年，從太宗平劉黑闥，陷陣有功。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Taizong in pacifying Liu Heita — breaking the battle lines with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he followed Taizong against Liu Heita and distinguished himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其誠節，賜姓李氏，拜右武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised his sincere integrity, bestowed the surname Li, and appointed him General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised his loyalty, granted him the surname Li, and made him General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was granted three hundred households of substantive enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he received an enfeoffment of three hundred tax households.

sentences.zh: 十一年，除婺州刺史，改封夷國公。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was removed from office to serve as Prefect of Wuzhou; his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of the State of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed prefect of Wuzhou and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，累轉黔州都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, through successive transfers he became Regional Commander of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing he rose through successive posts to military governor of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 以年老乞骸骨，許之，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Because of old age he requested dismissal and return of his bones; it was granted; he was advanced to Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to retire on grounds of age. The request was granted, and he was given the honorary title Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 麟德九年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth year of Linde.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Linde.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：蕭銑聚烏合之眾，當鹿走之時，放兵以奪將權，殺舊以求位定，洎大軍奄至，束手出降，宜哉！

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xiao Xian gathered a motley crowd; at the time when the deer ran free, he disbanded troops to seize generals' authority and killed old associates to secure his position — when the great army suddenly arrived, he bound his hands and surrendered; fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Xiao Xian rallied a rabble at the hour when the realm was up for grabs. He disbanded his armies to strip his generals of power and killed his old comrades to secure his throne. When the Tang armies arrived, he surrendered without a fight — as he deserved.

sentences.zh: 杜伏威恃勇聚徒，見機歸國，或致疑於高祖，竟見雪於太宗。

translations.literal: Du Fuwei relied on courage and gathered followers, saw the opportunity and returned to the state — he may have aroused suspicion in Emperor Gaozu, yet in the end was vindicated under the Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Du Fuwei, trusting in his courage, gathered followers and seized the moment to submit to the Tang. He may have aroused Gaozu's suspicion, but was ultimately vindicated under Taizong.

sentences.zh: 輔公祏竊兵為叛，王雄誕守節不回，訓子孫以忠貞，感士庶之流涕。

translations.literal: Fu Gongshi stole troops to rebel; Wang Xiongdan held to integrity and would not turn back, instructing his descendants in loyalty — moving gentry and commoners to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Gongshi seized the army and rebelled; Wang Xiongdan held firm and would not yield, leaving his descendants a lesson in loyalty that moved the people to tears.

sentences.zh: 子通修仁馭眾，終懷貳以伏誅；

translations.literal: Zitong cultivated benevolence to govern the multitude, yet in the end harbored disloyalty and suffered execution;
translations.idiomatic: Li Zitong governed his followers with benevolence, yet in the end turned disloyal and was executed;

sentences.zh: 羅藝歸國立功，信妖言而為叛。

translations.literal: Luo Yi returned to the state and achieved merit, yet believed demonic words and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Yi submitted to the Tang and won merit, then believed sorcerous prophecy and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 善始令終者，鮮矣！

translations.literal: Those who begin well and end well — how few!
translations.idiomatic: How few there are who begin well and end well!

sentences.zh: 沈法興狂賊，梁師都凶人，皆至覆亡，殊無改悔。

translations.literal: Shen Faxing was a mad bandit, Liang Shidu a vicious man — both reached ruin without the slightest repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Faxing was a mad rebel and Liang Shidu a vicious brute; both were destroyed without the slightest repentance.

sentences.zh: 自隋朝維絕，宇縣瓜分，小則鼠竊狗偷，大則鯨吞虎據。

translations.literal: From the time Sui's cords were cut, the realm was carved up — small cases were rat theft and dog snatching, great cases whale swallowing and tiger seizing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the fall of Sui, the realm was carved into fragments — petty rebels stole like rats and dogs, while great warlords seized territory like whales and tigers.

sentences.zh: 大唐舉義，兆庶歸仁，高祖運應瑤圖，太宗天資神武，群凶席捲，寰海鏡清，祚享永年，功宣後代，謚曰神堯、文武，豈不韙哉！

translations.literal: Great Tang raised the righteous cause, the myriad people returned to benevolence; Emperor Gaozu's fortune answered the jade chart, the Taizong's Heaven-given nature was divinely martial — all villains were swept away, the seas within the four borders mirror-clear; the throne enjoyed enduring years, merit proclaimed to later generations — posthumous titles Spirit-Yao and Civil-Martial; how fitting!
translations.idiomatic: When Great Tang raised the banner of righteousness, the people flocked to its benevolence. Gaozu's fortune matched Heaven's design; Taizong was divinely martial by nature. The rebels were swept away, and the realm was made mirror-clear. The dynasty was destined to endure, its achievements proclaimed to posterity — posthumous names Spirit-Yao and Civil-Martial. How fitting!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：失政資盜，圖王僭號。

translations.literal: Praise says: Lost government nourished bandits; they plotted kingship and presumptuous titles.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Misrule bred bandits who plotted thrones and usurped royal titles.

sentences.zh: 真主勃興，風驅電掃。

translations.literal: The true lord rose vigorously; wind drove and lightning swept them away.
translations.idiomatic: The true sovereign rose in power and swept them away like wind and lightning.
